entries.title: Identity & Tenancy
entries.content:
Identity & Tenancy

KeycloakInternal JWTPublic keysClaimsMembershipCedarControl planeReconcile loopWordThe sign-in server: it checks passwords and knows peopleA signed pass, made by claims-gateway, that every service trustsWhat anyone uses to check the pass is realWhat the pass says: who the person is, their organizations and rolesOne person in one organization, with one roleThe language access rules are written in, run inside each serviceServices that create organizations, not the product itselfA loop that looks at what should exist and makes it soMeaningLogin pageCookie authentication_tokenRead by IstioAda is staff in NorthfieldAda, staff, Northfield“staff may edit buildings”registry, provisionerEvery 15 sExample

Realises the Identity & Access domain. Four Go services plus Keycloak. Code-level pages: Claims Gateway, Tenancy, Registry, Provisioner.

-----

Who does what

Keycloakclaims-gatewaytenancyregistryprovisionerPartChecks the passwordTurns a Keycloak sign-in into the internal passOrganizations, memberships, invites, access rulesTakes a new customer’s signupTurns a signup into a working organizationJobPeopleNothingPostgreSQLPostgreSQLNothingKeeps

Each part does one job. Signing in and signing up change for different reasons, so they live in different services.



Solid: sign-in. Dotted: signup. registry and provisioner have no route at the edge: they are reached only from inside the network.

-----

Inside each service

All four have the same shape: a core with the rules, and adapters around it.



- Ports only on the way out. The core says “I need a store”, and a database or a fake fills it. Tests run with no database.
- No port on the way in. Each route has one real caller, so the handler calls the core directly.
- provisioner has a timer instead of HTTP handlers.

-----

Signing in



- Memberships are read once per sign-in, never per request.
- A first sign-in creates the membership, not the registration. So no single write has to touch Keycloak and tenancy together.
- Example. Ada’s Keycloak token names organization northfield, and she has no membership yet.
	- northfield is open to its sign-in server: Ada joins as a customer and gets a pass with it.
	- northfield is invite-only: tenancy refuses, and Ada still signs in, with no organization on her pass.
	- northfield does not exist in tenancy: sign-in fails with 503.

-----

Every later request

The edge checks the pass once. Services behind it trust the result.

Who checksExtra hop per requestWhat services receiveCaddy asks claims-gateway on every requestYesThe claims headerLocalIstio checks it alone, with the public keysNoThe same claims headerCluster

- Only claims-gateway ever checks a signature. Every other service reads the header and moves on.
- Same header both ways, so a service runs unchanged locally and in the cluster.

-----

How long a session lasts

Pass lifetimeclient renews itRenewing needsFact15 minEvery 10 min, with no user actionA pass that is still validValue

Example. Ada signs in at 09:00. The pass is renewed at 09:10, 09:20, and so on, all day. Her laptop sleeps from 10:05 to 10:30, and the pass dies at 10:20. On wake-up the renewal fails, and she signs in again.

Keep 10 below 15
-----
The two numbers live in different services, and nothing checks one against the other. A pass shorter than the renew interval ends every session.

-----

Access rules

- tenancy is the only Go service that runs Cedar. claims-gateway only identifies people. registry and provisioner work on organizations, which the rules do not cover.
- digital-twin, telemetry and agent run the same rules, from the same shared bundle.

Roles are flattened before Cedar runs. Cedar can test “is this in the list”, but not “is this role higher than that one”. So tenancy first turns each membership into lists:

Staff in NorthfieldAda’s membershipVisitor or higher: Northfield. Staff or higher: NorthfieldLists she ends up in

A rule then only asks “is this organization in the staff-or-higher list”.

“in” does not mean “in the list”
-----
In Cedar, in means “is a child of”, for entities. On a plain list it denies everything, with no error. Lists need “contains”. Only the shared tests that run real rules catch this.

Two checks stay outside Cedar, because they are not about roles:

- A person leaving an organization: is the target the caller?
- Auth turned off in dev and test: a setting, not a rule.

-----

Signing up



- The customer does not wait for the creation. A signup shows “provisioning” for up to one round.
- A repeat is safe: an organization that already exists counts as success.
- Who may join: anyone known to the customer’s own sign-in server, if the customer brought one. Invite only otherwise.
- No organization stays provisioning: each one ends ready or failed. A failed one is never tried again.

-----

Choices

Keycloak for every customerOne pass shape, frozen in a shared packageRules run inside each serviceOrganization in registry, tenant in tenancySignup by loop, not by callChoiceOne sign-in path, whatever the customer’s sizeEvery service reads it the same wayNo network call per decisionBilling and access change for different reasons, and are not always one to oneCreating an organization is slow, and nobody should wait for itWhy

-----

Gaps

- Only shared customers. Dedicated and on-premises signups end failed: no code builds them.
- No customer-owned sign-in per organization, and no self-service enterprise signup.
- Signup cannot be reached. registry takes a signup, but no edge route and no service calls it.
- A new organization has nobody in charge. provisioner creates the organization only, with no first admin, so nobody can invite the first member.
- A failed organization stays failed. Nothing tries it again.
- A missing organization blocks sign-in. A Keycloak token naming an organization tenancy does not know gives 503, every time.
- Only the first organization counts. A person in two Keycloak organizations is provisioned in the first only.
- A pass cannot be taken back. It lives its 15 minutes; nothing checks a revoked session.
- Internal signatures can be replayed. The HMAC covers the body only, not the method, path or time. Every internal GET with an empty body has the same signature, valid forever, for any accountId in its query.
- agent flattens roles its own way. It puts every organization in the lowest list whatever the role, so its decisions can differ from the shared test cases. See Auth Policy.
- A screen offline over 15 minutes stays signed out. client keeps no Keycloak refresh token, so it cannot sign in again alone.
- No metrics from any of the four services: a failing sign-in shows nowhere.
- Code vs domain: the domain has three roles. The code has four, with admin on top.

entries.title: Digital Twin
entries.content:
Digital Twin

TwinUploadWorkerPlacementTrackPortAdapterWordThe stored shape of a building: floors, rooms, sizesOne request to register a building, tracked until doneA loop inside the service that builds twins from a queueWhere one sensor or router sits in the buildingOne phone followed from tick to tickWhat the core needs from outside, said in its own wordsThe piece that does it with a real technologyMeaningNorthfield Library, 3 floorsStatus readyPicks the next uploadRouter on floor 1, by the stairsMoves from hall to room 2“store this building”MongoDBExample

Realises the Building Management domain. Rust, MongoDB. Code-level page: Digital Twin Service.

The source of truth for the shape of every building. Other services add live data on top of it.

-----

Who talks to it



Thin: a request. Thick: Kafka. Dotted: Redis.

It also calls three services directly:

telemetrydashboardnotificationToRoom limitsStarting columns“Upload failed”SendsAfter an editAfter registration, best effortWhen a registration failsWhen

BuildingsPlacementsWi-Fi estimateOwnership lookupJobRegister, read, list, change owner organizations, send again to telemetryWhere each sensor and router sitsWhere phones probably are, room by roomAnswers “which organizations own building X?” for the other servicesIn plain words

-----

Inside



- Entities hold what is true of a building whatever the storage, like “a room has a size above zero”.
- Use cases are the actions, like “register” or “update”, plus the ports they need.
- Access rules run in the core. “May Ada edit this building?” is a rule, and Cedar needs no network.
- Arrows point inward. Only the start-up code knows the store is MongoDB. Tests swap in fakes and need no database.
- A test fails the build if a layer imports the wrong way.

-----

Registering a building



Check before answeringAnswer before buildingAda polls the handleAnnounce on Kafka, do not callReady only on the answerStepA building the service would refuse is never acceptedBuilding is slow, and can fail for reasons Ada cannot fixShe sees ready or failed, never silencetelemetry can be down; the request waits for itSending the request is not success. telemetry saying “done” isWhy this way

- Three entries, one use case. HTTP, the worker and the Kafka answer all go through the same registration logic, so the three cannot drift apart.
- Twice is the same as once. A message can come twice. Building again ends in the same one building.
- Best effort extras. Starting columns in dashboard and room limits are sent after; a failure is logged, not fatal.

-----

Estimating phones from Wi-Fi

Each tick says which routers hear which phone, and how loud.



1. The floor is split into small cells. For each cell, the service knows how loud each router should sound there, walls included.
2. Each phone gets the cell that best matches what the routers heard.
3. A phone cannot jump faster than a person walks, so its last place narrows the choice.
4. A phone unseen for a few ticks is dropped. One missed poll does not end it.

Example. Router A hears a phone loud, router B faint. The cells near A and far from B score best. Last tick the phone was in room 2, next door, so room 2 wins over the hall beyond it.

- A tick older than three polls is skipped: it shows where people were, not where they are.
- Nothing is stored. Dots go to socket, room counts back to telemetry.

-----

Choices

The service makes building idsOwners come from the passShape treated as fixedSame size checks on every writeChoiceThe id never depends on what a client or a database choseNo call to identity services per requestOnly names and owners change; the live data lives elsewhereA bad room is refused with a clear error, never storedWhy

-----

Gaps

- Code vs domain: rooms cannot be edited. The domain says staff edit rooms. The code fixes them at upload.
- Code vs domain: starting Focus is a direct call to dashboard, best effort, not a reaction to “Building Ready”. If it fails, the building gets no live feed until someone saves its columns.
- The request rate limit lives in memory. Two copies of the service would each allow the full rate.

entries.title: Telemetry
entries.content:
Telemetry

ReadingTickMetricPluginMicrokernelLimitCollectorHMACWordOne value from one sensor at one momentEverything one building reports at one momentA kind of readingOne metric’s own rules, in one placeA small core that knows no metric, plus plugins that add themThe value a metric must stay withinA small box in the building that reads its Wi-Fi routersA signature that proves the sender holds the building’s keyMeaning24.5 °C in room 240 readings in one batchtemperature, peopleCountThe temperature pluginLike a phone and its appsOver 28 °C is a breachOne per siteSent with every batchExample

Realises the Telemetry Ingestion domain. Rust, PostgreSQL with TimescaleDB. Code-level page: Telemetry Service.

The door for every sensor reading. It checks, stores and hands on, and tells when a limit is broken.

-----

Who talks to it



Thin: a request. Thick: Kafka. Dotted: Redis.

With digital-twin it trades in both directions:

From digital-twinFrom digital-twinFrom digital-twinTo digital-twinTo digital-twinTo digital-twinDirectionNew building and its roomsRoom counts from Wi-FiRoom limits after an edit“Registration done”Wi-Fi ticks“Who owns this building?”WhatKafkaKafkaRequestKafkaKafkaRequestHow

-----

Two directions of change

Two things change often, and for different reasons. Each has its own pattern.

Kinds of metricTechnology around itWhat changesA new CO₂ sensorAnother database or brokerExampleMicrokernel: one new pluginPorts and adapters: one new adapterPattern



- The kernel never names a metric. It asks the registry for the right plugin. A new metric is one new plugin plus one line to register it.
- A plugin declares everything about its metric: fields, unit, limits, and the commands its devices accept.
- The catalog and the check read the same declaration. What telemetry says it accepts is exactly what it accepts.
- A test fails the build if the kernel imports a plugin or a technology, or a plugin imports another plugin.

-----

A batch comes in



One bad reading refuses the whole batchAt most 500 readingsStore before publishingPublishing never fails the batchBreaches are queued, not awaitedRuleThe sender knows exactly what was kept: all or nothingOne batch cannot hold the service upNobody sees a reading that cannot be queried yetThe reading is already safe; a broker hiccup is only loggedA Kafka outage cannot slow down sensorsWhy

Example. A batch holds 40 readings. Reading 17 has no room. The batch is refused, and none of the 40 is stored.

-----

Limits

- A limit is set for a building, and may be set for one room. The room’s limit wins.
- Registering a building sets every room’s limits in one request, all checked before any is written.
- deviceCount never raises a breach. A room full of laptops is not a crowd, and the Wi-Fi estimate is a guess. Crowding stays with peopleCount.

Example. The building limit for temperature is 28 °C. Room 2, a server room, has its own: 24 °C. A reading of 25 °C breaches in room 2 only.

-----

Wi-Fi ticks

1. The collector sends a signed tick: which router hears which phone.
2. telemetry refuses unknown fields, so a raw phone address cannot get in.
3. It counts phones per router room, each phone once, at its loudest router.
4. It hands the tick on to digital-twin, which estimates positions.
5. digital-twin sends room counts back, stored as readings like any other.

-----

Choices

One plugin per metricA port for every technologyAsk digital-twin who owns a buildingDevice commands in its own wordsChoiceA new sensor kind touches one placeThe kernel is tested with fakes, no databaseNo copy of someone else’s data to keep in step; a failed lookup deniesDevice URLs and fields live in one adapter only. See Sensor ActionsWhy

Storage and retention: Telemetry Storage.

-----

Gaps

- Code vs domain: one alert per breaching reading. The domain says one breach, one alert. The code sends a message per reading, and notification mutes repeats for 5 minutes, so a long breach alerts every 5 minutes.
- Code vs domain: no “Breach Ended”. Nothing is sent when a value comes back within its limit.

entries.title: Dashboard
entries.content:
Dashboard

TickFeedColumnsCatalogPub/subWordEverything one building reports at one momentThe live stream of one buildingWhich metrics a building’s table showsThe list of every metric the platform knowsSend to whoever listens now; nobody listening, message goneMeaningOne batch of readingsChannel for Northfield LibraryRoom name, max occupancy, temperaturetemperature, °C, from telemetryRedis channelExample

Realises part of the Telemetry Distribution domain, with socket. Rust, MongoDB. Code-level page: Dashboard Service.

Two jobs:

- Route every tick to its own building’s feed.
- Remember each building’s columns, and collect the metric catalog.

-----

Who talks to it



Dotted: Redis. Thin: a request.

-----

Inside

No layers on purpose: there is no domain logic to protect. Two loops share one in-memory map.



- The router loop reads the map on every tick. The database is never on that path.
- A column change is in the map at once, so the next tick already sees it.
- The two loops never call each other. The map is all they share.

-----

Routing a tick



- Only the building id is read. The bytes go on exactly as received.
- Every metric goes through. Columns decide what the table shows, in the browser, not what flows. So the 3D view stays live whatever the table shows.
- A tick never reaches another building’s channel.

Example. Northfield Library shows 2 columns, but its sensors send 5 metrics. All 5 reach the browser. The table shows 2, the 3D view colours rooms by any of the 5.

-----

Columns

- A new building starts with two: room name and max occupancy. Starting again keeps the columns it has.
- Saving answers at once, then writes to MongoDB in the background. A failed write is only logged.

-----

Catalog

- dashboard does not define metrics. It asks each source for its own list and merges them.
- Sources come from settings, so a new one needs no code change.
- A slow or broken source gives an empty list after 2 s. The catalog never fails as a whole.

-----

Gaps

- A building with no columns gets no live feed. Its ticks are dropped. Starting columns come from a best effort call by digital-twin, so a failed call leaves a building dark until someone saves columns.
- A saved column can be lost. The answer comes before MongoDB has it. On a restart, the map is rebuilt from what MongoDB holds.

entries.title: Socket
entries.content:
Socket

WebSocketRoomSubscribeClaims headerFunctional coreImperative shellWordA connection the browser keeps open, so the server can pushA group of connections that get the same messagesA browser asks to join one building’s roomWho the caller is, set by the edgePlain functions with no network, easy to testThe part that does the network work around the coreMeaningOne per open tabbuilding:{id}, domain:{name}Opening the library pagex-gateway-claims“which room is this message for?”Redis, WebSocketExample

Realises part of the Telemetry Distribution domain, with dashboard: it carries live data to the people following a building. Rust, no database. Code-level page: Socket Service.

-----

Who talks to it



Dotted: Redis.

A building’s feednotificationsA building’s device dotsComes in onbuilding:{id}domain:{name}building:{id}Goes to roomtelemetrynotificationDevice positionsBrowser event

Messages pass through unread, apart from finding the room.

-----

Inside



- The core does no network work, so it is tested with plain inputs.
- A test fails the build if the core imports a network library, or names the shell.
- Room names and the header name are written in one place each, so they cannot drift.

-----

Connecting and subscribing



- Joining the room is the permission check. Every message to that room then goes out with no further check.
- Organization rooms come from the claims at connect. Building rooms need a subscribe each.

Owners foundNo owners, or unknown buildingLookup failedOwnership answerYesYesNoKept for 60 s?Join if an organization is sharedRefusedRefused, the next try asks againResult

- Caching “unknown” stops a client from guessing ids to flood digital-twin.
- Not caching failures means a short digital-twin hiccup does not blank screens for a minute.
- Refusals are counted apart: a stranger knocking and digital-twin down must not look the same.

-----

How long a connection lives

- At most about 15 minutes, like the pass. Then socket closes it.
- Each connection gets a little less, at random, up to an eighth. Otherwise every client from one deploy would reconnect in the same second, forever.
- client reconnects after a short wait, with a fresh cookie. That reconnect is the new identity check.
- After a reconnect, client subscribes to its buildings again and fetches the gap.

Example. The permission check runs only at subscribe. Ada leaves Northfield at 10:00. Her open tab keeps getting library data until its connection is closed, at most about 15 minutes later.

-----

Choices

No domain model, no databaseTrust the edge’s claimsBuilding data per building room, alerts per organization roomA message with no organization is skippedChoiceIt only carries messages; it can be replaced at any timeThe edge already checked the pass; no second checkNo organization sees another’s dataSending it to everyone would leak names across customersWhy

-----

Gaps

- One copy only. More copies would need sticky sessions and a shared adapter so every copy hears every room.
- A connection can outlive its pass by up to its lifetime. The pass carries no end time a connection could check.

entries.title: Notification
entries.content:
Notification

BreachAlertCooldownWeb PushPush subscriptionDead-letter topicSystem callerWordA value outside its limitWhat a person receives about a breachA pause during which repeats of one alert are mutedBrowser notifications that arrive with no tab openOne device’s address for Web PushWhere messages that cannot be handled waitA service calling with no person behind itMeaning31 °C, limit 28 °C“Room 2 is too hot”5 minutes per room and fieldPhone lock screenAda’s laptopalerts.dlqsystem:notification-serviceExample

Realises the Alerting domain. Rust, MongoDB, Redis. Code-level page: Notification Service.

Decides who should hear about a breach, then tells them twice: in the app and by Web Push.

-----

Who talks to it



Thick: Kafka. Thin: a request. Dotted: Redis.

Two things it keeps, kept apart:

DevicesChoicesKeptWhere each person can be reachedWhat each person wants to hearHoldsA lost phone is removed without losing choicesChoices change without registering devices againWhy apart

-----

Inside



Two ways in, one alert logic. A test alert and a real breach go through the same steps.

-----

A breach becomes an alert



Lookup failed: not mutedNo owner: mutedNever sent with no organizationCaseThe alert can be sent again once digital-twin is backEvery following tick would flood the log otherwiseIt would reach every browser of every customerWhy

Example. Room 2 reads 31 °C every 10 s, limit 28 °C. The first breach alerts at 10:00:00. The next 29 are muted. The one at 10:05:00 alerts again.

Watch the “failed” and “unroutable” counts: either means an alert reached nobody.

-----

Finding the owners

- notification asks digital-twin and keeps no copy of buildings.
- The lookup gives up after 2 s. A stuck digital-twin must not hold every alert behind it.
- Answers are kept 15 minutes. An empty answer or a failure is never kept, so a building that just finished registering is found on the next alert.
- Why 15 minutes and not more: a building moved to another organization keeps alerting the old one until the entry expires. Longer saves almost nothing, since the cooldown already limits lookups.

socket keeps the same answer only 60 s. Different question: it decides who may read live data, so it needs to be fresher.

-----

Who may receive

A person, through the test routeA system callerCallerOwner organizations they belong to, nothing elseEvery owner organizationGets alerts for

A system caller has no memberships. Filtering would drop everything, and the failed-upload alert from digital-twin would vanish. Only services inside the mesh can be a system caller: the edge strips the claims header from outside requests.

The system identity keeps an older name, system:notification-service, on purpose. It is checked byte for byte at a trust boundary.

-----

Web Push

- A device the push provider calls gone, with 410 or 403, is removed on the next send. No cleanup job needed.

-----

Gaps

- alerts.dlq has no reader. Parked alerts wait there until someone replays them by hand.
- Code vs domain: a long breach alerts every 5 minutes, not once. See Telemetry.

entries.title: Chat
entries.content:
Chat

ConversationExchangeHistory windowSSEFrameWordOne person’s thread of questions and answersOne question and its answerThe last messages sent along with a new questionServer-Sent Events: the answer arrives word by word on one open responseOne piece of that streamMeaning“Library heating”“Is room 2 hot?” and the replyLast 10Text appearing as it is writtenA word, or “done”Example

Realises the Knowledge & Assistance domain, with agent. Rust, MongoDB. Code-level page: Chat Service.

chat remembers conversations. agent answers one question at a time and remembers nothing. Together they make a conversation.

-----

Who talks to it



-----

Inside



Two things outside, so two ports. A test fails the build if a layer imports the wrong way.

-----

Asking a question



Only the last 10 messages go alongStream, do not waitSave only at the endForward the same claimsRuleA long conversation does not grow the cost of each questionThe first words show in milliseconds, not secondsA broken answer leaves no half message behindagent acts with the person’s own rights, no moreWhy

Errors depend on timing. Before the first word: a normal error status, like 404. After: the status line is already sent as 200, so the error comes as a last frame.

-----

Limits

Messages per conversationCharacters per messageCharacters per titleWhat1008000120Limit

Checked before anything is saved.

- A new conversation is called “New chat”. The first question becomes its title after the first answer.
- Every action checks owner and conversation together. Someone else’s conversation answers “not found”, so its existence does not leak.
- The edge must not hold the stream back. Caddy needs flush_interval -1 on /chat.

entries.title: Agent
entries.content:
Agent

LLMToolHopChunkEmbeddingCitationTraceWordThe language model that writes the answerSomething the model may ask the service to doOne round: the model answers, or asks for a toolA small piece of the documentation, searched on its ownA list of numbers that stands for a text’s meaningA pointer from the answer to the chunk it came fromA record of every hop and tool, with time and costMeaningAny OpenAI-compatible providerRead a building’s sensorsHop 1 asks for sensors, hop 2 answersOne section of a pageUsed to find similar chunks[1]Sent to LangfuseExample

Realises the Knowledge & Assistance domain, with chat. Python, PostgreSQL with pgvector. Code-level page: Agent Service.

Answers one question at a time: finds the right documentation, fetches live data if needed, writes an answer with citations. Remembers nothing between questions.

-----

Who talks to it



-----

Inside



- Model, embeddings and reranking are ports. A provider changes behind them, the loop does not.
- Tools are plugins, like metrics in telemetry. The loop never knows which tool it calls; it asks the registry by name.

-----

The loop



Example. “Is room 2 too hot?” Hop 1: the model asks for room 2’s sensors. Hop 2: with 31 °C in hand, it answers, citing the limits page.

A hop limitCitations checked after writingStreamed and waited answers share one loopThe final answer wins over streamed wordsRuleA model stuck calling tools cannot spend time and money foreverA citation to a chunk never retrieved is removed, not shownThe two cannot drift; only the model call differsRemoved citations may already have been streamedWhy

-----

Finding documentation



- Both searches filter by the person’s rights inside the query. A chunk the person may not read never reaches the model.

-----

Rights, checked twice

SearchToolsWhereWhich documentation the person may readWhich live data the person may read, with CedarChecks

Neither layer trusts the other to have checked.

- No admin shortcut. An admin outside an organization is refused its data.
- Choosing another model costs money, so it needs a high enough role, set by the operator. Without it: 403, never a silent fallback.
- Auth turned off in dev and test lets everyone in. That is a setting, checked before Cedar.

-----

How it is reached

- /agent is open at the edge, so evals can call it with their own test token.
- Both edges strip any claims header on /agent. Otherwise an outside caller could forge one.
- It is the service that turns model output into calls, so it gets the most care. In the cluster, it is the one service with an Istio rule limiting who may call it.
- People reach agent through chat, which forwards claims the edge has checked.

-----

Gaps

- No Prometheus metrics. Traces go to Langfuse only.
- The reranker does nothing yet. Results are the merged ranking.

entries.title: Auth Contracts
entries.content:
Auth Contracts

Go moduleClaimsMembershipRole weightRole ladderHMACGolden vectorMiddlewareWordA Go library other Go code importsWhat the token says about the callerOne domain the caller belongs to, with one role thereA number that ranks roles: higher means more powerAll roles with their weightsA signature made with a secret both sides holdA fixed input with its known right answer, checked by every languageCode that runs before a route handler and can stop the requestMeaningbackend/libs/auth-contractssub, accountName, memberships{domain: "unibo", role: "standard_customer"}business_admin = 80roles.jsonX-Signature: bd3ae5…secret + body → signatureRequireSignatureExample

Go module at backend/libs/auth-contracts. It holds three things every Go service must agree on:

claims.goroles.go + roles.jsoninternalsig.goFileStandardClaims, MembershipRoleWeights, Can()Sign, Verify, RequireSignatureHoldsThe shape of the caller, same in every serviceOne ranking of roles, read by every languageOne way for a service to prove “this call is from another CrowdVision service”Why shared

Standard library only: no outside dependency. registry and provisioner need the signature code but never check a token, so this module must not pull in JWT libraries.

-----

Who uses what

StandardClaimsMembershipRoleWeightsCan()roles.json, read as a fileSignRequireSignatureItemclaims-gateway signer.Sign, auth-middlewareclaims-gateway tenancyclient, tenancy MembershipsFor, auth-policyclaims-gateway exchange.go, tenancy service and handler, auth-policy accountEntitytenancy service/tenancy.godigital-twin service/authz.rs, telemetry kernel/authz.rs, notification domain/identity.rs (include_str!); agent app/roles.py (at start-up)provisioner (both clients), claims-gateway tenancyclientregistry and tenancy /internal/* routesUsed byBuild the token; read it backCarry memberships between servicesPick the strongest role; compare roles“Is this role at least business_admin?”Same ladder outside GoSign an internal callCheck an internal callFor

RoleIn, CanIn and Tenants on StandardClaims have no caller outside this module’s tests. tenancy has its own roleIn in internal/api/handler.go, which keeps the highest role when one domain appears twice.

-----

1. StandardClaims

Shape

	{"sub":"8f1c2e3a-4b5d-4e6f-9a1b-2c3d4e5f6a7b","accountName":"mario",
	 "sid":"b2a9c1d0-1234-4e6f-9a1b-2c3d4e5f6a7b",
	 "memberships":[{"domain":"unibo","role":"standard_customer","externalId":"eppn:mario@unibo.it"}]}

subaccountNamesidmembershipsexternalIdJSONSubAccountNameSIDMembershipsMembership.ExternalIDGo fieldAccount id. Every access decision keys on itName shown to peopleSession id. signer.Sign makes a new UUID when emptyList of {domain, role, externalId}The identity provider’s id for this membership. Left out of JSON when emptyMeaning

The type has no field for a tier or an identity provider. A direct sign-up and a federated one reach every service in this same shape.

Helper methods

RoleIn(domain)CanIn(domain, required)Tenants()MethodRole in that domain, and whether one exists. First match winsRoleIn, then CanEvery domain, in membership orderGivesRoleIn("acme") = business_admin, trueCanIn("unibo", "business_admin") = false["acme", "unibo"]Example, with acme: business_admin, unibo: standard_customer

-----

2. The role ladder

Data

roles.json, embedded in the binary with //go:embed:

adminbusiness_adminbusiness_staffstandard_customerRole100806010Weight

- Read once at start-up into RoleWeights. Invalid JSON makes the program panic at start: a service never runs with a broken ladder.
- Embedded at build time, so a running Go service cannot read a different file than the one it was built with.

How Can(have, need) decides



Can("admin", "business_admin")Can("business_admin", "business_admin")Can("standard_customer", "business_admin")Can("not-a-role", "standard_customer")Can("business_admin", "not-a-role")Call100 ≥ 8080 ≥ 8010 ≥ 80unknownunknownWeightstruetruefalsefalsefalseResultHigher passesEqual passesLower failsUnknown caller role deniesA typo in the required role denies. Reading it as weight 0 would let everyone throughWhy

Where the ladder is read



One file, five readers, no copy. Changing a weight changes every language at the next build or start.

-----

3. Internal signatures

Some calls carry no person: provisioner setting up a new organization acts for nobody, so there is no claims header to forward. These calls prove who sent them with an HMAC over the body.

The rule

- Header: X-Signature.
- Value: lowercase hex of HMAC-SHA256, key = shared secret (INTERNAL_SIGNING_SECRET), message = the exact request body bytes.
- An empty body is signed too: a GET signs zero bytes.
- Verify compares with hmac.Equal, which takes the same time whatever the input, so timing leaks nothing.

Who signs, who checks

provisioner registryclientprovisioner registryclientprovisioner tenancyclientclaims-gateway tenancyclientclaims-gateway tenancyclientCallerSign(secret, nil)Sign(secret, raw)Sign(secret, body)Sign(secret, nil)Sign(secret, body)FunctionGET /internal/organizations/pending on registryPOST /internal/organizations/{id}/status on registryPOST /internal/domains on tenancyGET /internal/memberships?accountId=… on tenancyPOST /internal/provision on tenancyRoute on the receiveremptyJSONJSONemptyJSONBody

registry also has POST /internal/organizations/{id}/suspend behind the same check.

A signed call end to end



Data at each step

Example from the shared fixture schemas/fixtures/internal-signature.json: secret an-internal-secret-that-is-at-least-32-bytes.

13467911StepBody {"buildingId":"bldg-1","status":"ready"} (40 bytes)Signature bd3ae57b5d5672d04b5c376ddd2b2fe60a348a9c5d151d631d6fd38241772418Header X-Signature: bd3ae57b…2418, same 40 bytes as bodyThose 40 bytes in memoryA new reader over the same 40 bytes, so the handler can read themRecomputed signature, equal to step 3Handler sees the original bodyData

A body with one extra space gives a different signature, so step 9 fails with 403.

Why each check gives its status

No X-SignatureBody cannot be readWrong signatureCase403400403StatusNot a known serviceThe connection broke. Saying 403 would tell the caller its secret is wrong when it is notWrong secret, or the body changed on the wayWhy

Same rule outside Go

telemetry checks device batches with its own Rust code (adapters/ingest_auth.rs) and its own key. Both sides check the same golden vectors in schemas/fixtures/internal-signature.json:

empty bodyjson bodyunicodeCase(nothing){"buildingId":"bldg-1","status":"ready"}{"name":"Aula Magna — Cesena"}Body52a0b3efbd3ae57b2ec44f60Signature starts

Change the algorithm on one side and the other side’s test fails.

-----

Tests

roles_test.goclaims_test.goconformance_test.gointernalsig_test.goTestHigher and equal pass; lower denied; unknown caller role denied; unknown required role denied; weights are 100, 80, 60, 10RoleIn finds the role and misses a foreign domain; CanIn is scoped to one domain; Tenants orderschemas/fixtures/standard-claims.json parses into StandardClaims, has sub, accountName, sid, at least one membership, and every role is on the ladderEvery golden vector signs and verifies; a one-byte change, another secret, an empty signature all fail; the handler still reads the body; missing or wrong signature is 403; an unreadable body is 400 and the handler never runsChecks

The same claims fixture is checked by Rust (schemas/claims-schema/tests/conformance.rs) and Python (agent/tests/unit/test_claims_conformance.py).

	mise exec -- go test ./...   # in backend/libs/auth-contracts

-----

Gaps

- The signature covers the body only. Method, path and time are not signed. Every empty-body GET with one secret has the same signature, so a captured one works on any GET /internal/* route behind that secret, forever.
- Go does not check the secret’s length. telemetry refuses a key under 32 bytes; the Go services accept any non-empty INTERNAL_SIGNING_SECRET.
- RoleIn, CanIn, Tenants have no caller. RoleIn keeps the first match, while tenancy’s own roleIn keeps the highest. Two answers to one question.

entries.title: Claims Schema
entries.content:
Claims Schema

CrateClaims headerBase64 alphabetExtractorLenientFixtureWordA Rust library other Rust code builds againstx-gateway-claims: the checked token’s claims, base64-encoded, added by the edgeThe 64 characters base64 uses, and whether it pads with =Axum code that builds a value from a request before the handler runsKeeps what it can read instead of failing the whole thingA JSON file of example messages every language must agree onMeaningclaims-schemaeyJzdWIiOiJ1MSJ9standard uses + /, URL-safe uses - _GatewayClaimsa bad membership is droppedschemas/fixtures/standard-claims.jsonExample

Rust crate at schemas/claims-schema. It reads the x-gateway-claims header for every Rust service. Go has the same job in Auth Contracts, Python in agent/app/auth.py: one reader per language, never one per service.

Depends only on serde, serde_json, base64. No I/O, no web framework.

-----

Who uses it

digital-twintelemetrydashboardchatnotificationsocketServiceClaimsPayload, Membership, CLAIMS_HEADER, decode_claims_headersameClaimsPayload::decode, CLAIMS_HEADERClaimsPayload, CLAIMS_HEADER, decode_claims_headersame as digital-twinClaimsPayload::decode, CLAIMS_HEADERImportssub required, else 401 Invalid authentication tokensub requiredsub required, else bare 401sub required, else 401 …missing an account idaccountName required, else 401 …missing an accountsub and accountName required, else the connection is refusedRule its extractor adds

The crate only reads. Deciding which field is required is each service’s job, because the services need different things: notification keys subscriptions by account name, the others key on sub.

-----

Shape

	pub const CLAIMS_HEADER: &str = "x-gateway-claims";
	pub struct Membership {
	    pub domain: String,
	    pub role: Option<String>,
	    pub external_id: Option<String>,   // "externalId"
	}
	pub struct ClaimsPayload {
	    pub sub: Option<String>,
	    pub account_name: Option<String>,  // "accountName"
	    pub sid: Option<String>,
	    pub memberships: Vec<Membership>,
	}

Field for field the same as Go’s StandardClaims. Every field is optional in the type: parsing says what the header says, the service says whether that is enough.

-----

A request end to end

digital-twin’s extractor, adapters/driving/http_api/claims.rs; the others follow the same steps.



Data at each step

Header for {"sub":"u1","accountName":"ada","memberships":[{"domain":"acme","role":"business_admin"},"beta"]}, sent URL-safe without padding.

156891112Stepx-gateway-claims: eyJzdWIiOiJ1MSIs… (no = at the end)STANDARD fails on the missing padding; URL_SAFE fails too; STANDARD_NO_PAD succeedsThe JSON bytes above"beta" is not an object: dropped. memberships = [{acme, business_admin}]ClaimsPayload { sub: Some("u1"), account_name: Some("ada"), sid: None, memberships: [1 entry] }Some("u1")GatewayClaims with the payload and the raw header, kept so the service can forward itData

-----

Two reading choices

Four base64 alphabets

decode_claims_header tries four decoders in order and keeps the first that works:

1234OrderSTANDARD (+ /)URL_SAFE (- _)STANDARD_NO_PADURL_SAFE_NO_PADAlphabetrequiredrequirednonenonePadding

A Rust decoder accepts exactly one form. The edge may write any of them, so trying only one would refuse good headers.

Bad memberships are dropped, not fatal



Example. ["acme", {"domain":7}, {"role":"admin"}, {"domain":"beta"}] keeps only beta, with no role.

Why: failing the whole header turns “not a member of that domain” (403) into “broken token” (401). The person debugging then looks in the wrong service. A memberships that is not a list at all is still fatal: that is a broken token.

-----

Accessors

decode(header)user_id()account()session_id()domains()role_in(domain)belongs_to(domain)has_role(role)Methoddecode_claims_header then JSON parse; None on either failuresub, trimmed; None when missing or blankaccountName, trimmed, same rulesid, same ruleEvery membership’s domainRole of the first membership with that domaintrue when a membership has that domain; always false for ""true when any membership has that role, in any domainGives{"sub":"   "} gives None{"sid":""} gives None["acme", "unibo"]role_in("acme") = Some("business_admin")belongs_to("") = falseExample

A blank string is treated as missing, so "   " can never act as an identity.

-----

What stays in each service

- The extractor and its error type. Axum’s FromRequestParts is a trait from another crate, and Rust forbids implementing it for this crate’s types from a service. The error types also differ: StatusCode in dashboard, DomainError in the others.
- Access rules. Cedar entities, the system: callers, which field is required. A shape crate that grows rules ties every service to every other.

-----

Tests

src/lib.rstests/conformance.rstests/tenancy_domains_schema.rstests/chat_conversation_schema.rsTestAll four alphabets decode; not-base64 and not-JSON fail; the full contract round trips; blank fields are None; missing or null memberships give an empty list; bad entries dropped; a non-list fails; roles scoped per domain; a membership with no role still grants the domainstandard-claims.json parses with sub, accountName, sid, role, externalId; written back it equals the fixture, so no field is silently lost; it matches schemas/json/standard-claims.schema.json; the schema refuses a role off the ladder (emperor)Fixture-against-schema for tenancy-domains.json, a shape between tenancy and the frontend with no Rust typeSame for chat-conversation.json, which only chat writes and the frontend readsChecks

The same claims fixture is checked by Go (backend/libs/auth-contracts/conformance_test.go) and Python (agent/tests/unit/test_claims_conformance.py). Socket, notification and chat also have an architecture test that the header name is claims_schema::CLAIMS_HEADER, never a literal.

	mise exec -- cargo test --manifest-path schemas/claims-schema/Cargo.toml

-----

Building a service that uses it

The dependency is a path, ../../schemas/claims-schema, so each consumer image builds from the repo root (cd_context: "." in .github/services.json). Each Dockerfile copies the crate before cargo chef prepare and before each cargo chef cook; a path missing during cook fails the build half way.

-----

Gaps

- The other languages accept fewer alphabets. Go’s RequireMeshClaims takes standard base64 only, and Python’s agent/app/auth.py uses base64.b64decode, also standard. A header these four alphabets accept in Rust can be refused in tenancy or agent.
- role_in takes the first match. If one domain appears twice with two roles, Rust and Go’s RoleIn give the first, while tenancy’s own roleIn gives the highest.

entries.title: Twin Schema
entries.content:
Twin Schema

CrateRegistrationUploadWi-Fi tickTokenBurstdBmDotTopicChannelFixtureWordA Rust library other Rust code builds againstdigital-twin telling telemetry that a building exists, and telemetry answeringOne request to register a building, tracked until ready or failedWhat one building’s routers saw at one moment16 hex characters that stand for one phone in one tick, made at random on siteA phone’s scan for networks, heard by one or more routersSignal strength. Closer to 0 is louderOne estimated person, drawn on the 3D modelA Kafka name that messages are stored onA Redis name that messages are published onA JSON file of example messages every language must agree onMeaningtwin-schema“b1 is ready”handle b13 routers, 2 phones7f3c9a01b2d4e6f8heard at −58 and −71 dBm−40 loud, −90 faintLobby, floor 0wifi-observationstwin:devices:b1schemas/fixtures/devices.jsonExample

Rust crate at schemas/twin-schema. It holds every shape digital-twin exchanges with another service, and the topic and channel names they travel on.

Depends only on serde and serde_json. Tests also use jsonschema.

-----

What is inside

RegistrationRequestRegistrationCompletedWifiObservationsDevices, DeviceEstimatedOccupancyShapeKafka building-registration-requestedKafka building-registration-completedHTTP POST /telemetry/observations, then Kafka wifi-observationsRedis twin:devices:{buildingId}Kafka estimated-occupancyTravels ondigital-twintelemetryap-collector (Python)digital-twindigital-twinWritten bytelemetrydigital-twintelemetry, digital-twinsocket, browsertelemetryRead by

BUILDING_REGISTRATION_REQUESTED_TOPICBUILDING_REGISTRATION_COMPLETED_TOPICSTATUS_READY, STATUS_FAILEDWIFI_OBSERVATIONS_TOPICESTIMATED_OCCUPANCY_TOPICDEVICES_CHANNEL_PREFIXDEVICES_CHANNEL_PATTERNNamebuilding-registration-requestedbuilding-registration-completedready, failedwifi-observationsestimated-occupancytwin:devices:twin:devices:*Value

Each service re-exports the topic names from its own adapters/topics.rs. The text of a topic name is written once, here.



Thin: HTTP or Redis. Thick: Kafka.

-----

1. Registration

Shapes

	{"buildingId":"b1","name":"HQ","rooms":[{"id":"r1","name":"Lobby"},{"id":"r2","name":"Lab"}]}

	{"buildingId":"b1","status":"failed","error":"name: must be a non-empty string."}

buildingIdnamemaxTemperatureroomsRegistrationRequest fieldOptional in the type, left out when empty. digital-twin always sends it; telemetry drops a message without itEmpty when missing, so telemetry’s own check gives the error text, not serdeOptional. digital-twin never sends it. telemetry still reads it and, when present, stores a building temperature limitRead by usable_rooms, belowRule

buildingIdstatuserrorRegistrationCompleted fieldRequiredPlain text, not a closed listLeft out when emptyRule

The handshake, call by call



Data at each step

Example: building b1 named HQ, rooms r1 Lobby and r2 with a blank name.

278101314Step{"buildingId":"b1","name":"HQ","rooms":[{"id":"r1","name":"Lobby"},{"id":"r2","name":"r2"}]}RegistrationRequest, max_temperature None, 2 rooms1 building row, 2 room rows in telemetry’s database. No limit written{"buildingId":"b1","status":"ready"}failure() gives Nonethe upload b1 becomes readyData

Reading rooms leniently

usable_rooms reads rooms as a list of plain JSON values and keeps what it can:



Example. [{"name":"ghost"}, {"id":""}, "r0", {"id":"r1"}] gives one room: r1, named r1.

Why: a room with no id cannot be stored or found again. Failing the whole building for one such room would refuse a building for a room nobody can use anyway.

Reading the answer

failure() turns the answer into “done” or a reason:



Example. {"buildingId":"b1","status":"exploded"} reads as a failure with reason exploded.

Why status is text and not an enum: an unknown value would then fail to parse. A message that fails to parse is logged and skipped, so the upload would stay pending for ever. As text, anything that is not ready fails the upload, with a reason.

Who decides failed

telemetry answers failed only when the request itself is wrong: no name, a NUL character, a maxTemperature that is not a number. A database error in telemetry is not answered: the message is read again later. Answering failed would make digital-twin delete the building.

-----

2. The Wi-Fi tick

Shape

	{"buildingId":"bldg-3f2b4c5d","tick":1761300000000,
	 "answered":["e6f7…","f708…","0819…"],
	 "connected":[{"token":"7f3c9a01b2d4e6f8","router":"e6f7…","signal":-61},
	              {"token":"c2d4e6f8091a2b3c","router":"f708…","signal":-70},
	              {"token":"c2d4e6f8091a2b3c","router":"0819…","signal":-72}],
	 "bursts":[{"token":"a91e0c3d5f7b2846","started":1761299998412,
	            "heard":{"e6f7…":-58,"f708…":-71,"0819…":-80}}]}

Router ids are UUIDs, cut here.

buildingIdtickansweredconnectedburstsdevicesPerPersonFieldThe building whose key signed the tickWhen the collector took the snapshot, ms since 1970Routers that replied. A router missing here failed: its phones are unknown, not goneOne row per router listing a phone. One token on two rows is one phone heard twiceScans heard: token, start time in ms, and each router’s loudest signal. Always present, empty when scanning is offOptional. Phones per person for this site; without it, no people estimateMeaning

No MAC address and no coordinates ever: tokens are random per tick, positions belong to digital-twin.

The rules, in two places

serde, deny_unknown_fieldsproblems()problems()problems()problems()problems()problems()problems()Checked byNo extra field anywhere. A mac beside a token failsbuildingId not emptyEach router in answered once, not emptydevicesPerPerson, when present, finite and above 0At most 2000 connected rows (MAX_CONNECTED), 2000 bursts (MAX_BURSTS)Token: exactly 16 characters, 0–9 and a–fSignal from −127 (MIN_SIGNAL) to 0 dBm, router not emptyA burst heard by 1 to 6 routers (MAX_HEARD)Rule

problems() returns one message per broken rule, empty when the tick is sound. The limits keep a tick of UUID router ids under telemetry’s 1 MiB body limit.

Why no extra fields: telemetry forwards the received bytes to Kafka. An unchecked field would travel with them.

A tick end to end



digital-twin runs problems() again: it does not take the broker’s word for it.

Example, step 4. Phone c2d4… is on two routers at −70 and −72 dBm. It counts once, in the room of the −70 router. Phone 7f3c… counts in its router’s room. Result: 2 phones, in up to 2 rooms.

-----

3. Devices for the browser

Shape

	{"buildingId":"bldg-3f2b4c5d","tick":1761300000000,"devices":[
	  {"floor":0,"room":"room-lobby","x":4.25,"y":0.0,"z":6.5,"radius":2.1,"connected":true},
	  {"floor":1,"room":"room-office","x":12.75,"y":3.5,"z":3.25,"radius":5.4,"connected":false}]}

buildingIdtickdevicesfloorroomx, y, zradiusconnectedFieldMust match the channel’s buildingThe snapshot these dots come fromEvery dot of this tick. Always present; an empty list clears the buildingFloor index, lowest firstRoom idPosition in model metres. y is the floor’s heightOne spread of the position, metresfalse for someone passing who never joined the Wi-FiMeaning

Device has deny_unknown_fields: no token, MAC or id can ride on a dot.

Channel names

devices_channel("b1")building_of_devices_channel("twin:devices:site:b1")building_of_devices_channel("twin:devices:")building_of_devices_channel("notifications")Functiontwin:devices:b1Some("site:b1")None: no buildingNone: not a devices channelGives

Dots end to end



At step 6 socket skips the message when the channel names no building, the body is not a Devices, or the two building ids differ.

-----

4. Room counts for telemetry

	{"buildingId":"bldg-3f2b4c5d","tick":1761300000000,"rooms":{"room-lobby":3,"room-office":0}}

One message per accepted tick, only when at least one router answeredEvery room on a floor with a placed router, zeros includedConnected dots onlyCounts only, deny_unknown_fieldsTopic keyed by buildingId, kept 1 h, created by digital-twinRuleNo answer would record an empty building that is not emptydigital-twin can place no one on a floor with no routerA passing dot is placed too rarely to countNo position can ride alongAn hour of history survives a telemetry restartWhy

telemetry stores each room as an estimatedOccupancy reading at the tick’s time (kernel/occupancy.rs). It never touches totalDeviceCount, which is telemetry’s own count.

Example. The message above becomes two readings at 1761300000000: room-lobby 3, room-office 0.

-----

What stays out of this crate

Building, Room, Coordinates, Dimensions stay in digital-twin/src/domain/. No other Rust service parses them: the ownership lookup GET /domain/{building} answers a plain list of domain names.

The full building is read by agent (Python) and the frontend (TypeScript). A fixture holds them in line:

RustPythonSchemaLanguagedigital-twin/tests/building_conformance.rs: parses schemas/fixtures/building.json into the real Building, writes it back, comparesagent/tests/unit/test_building_conformance.py: runs the same file through the projections the twin tools give the modeltwin-schema/tests/building_schema.rs: the fixture against schemas/json/building.schema.jsonTest

-----

Tests

Rejected Wi-Fi cases in the fixture: a MAC as token, a MAC beside the token, coordinates on a burst, a positive signal, a burst no router heard, a burst heard by seven routers, a start in seconds, no answered, devicesPerPerson 0, a router answering twice.

entries.title: Telemetry Schema
entries.content:
Telemetry Schema

CrateShapeSerialiseDeserialise, parseTickReadingBreachFixtureChannelTopicWordA Rust library other Rust code builds againstThe fields a JSON message carries, and their namesTurn a Rust value into JSON textTurn JSON text back into a Rust value, or failEverything one building reports at one momentOne value from one room at one momentA value past its limitA JSON file of example messages every language must agree onA Redis name that messages are published onA Kafka name that messages are stored onMeaningtelemetry-schema{buildingId, ingestedAt, readings}TelemetryEnvelope → {"buildingId":"b1",…}A missing buildingId fails40 readings in one message21.5 °C in room r11200 ppm CO₂, limit 1000schemas/fixtures/telemetry-envelope.jsontelemetry:filtered:b1alertsExample

Rust crate at schemas/telemetry-schema. It holds every telemetry shape that crosses from one service to another, so the service that writes a message and the service that reads it build from one definition.

Depends only on serde and serde_json. Tests also use jsonschema.

-----

Why one crate

Two services that each declare their own copy of a shared shape drift apart without any error. It happened once:

- telemetry sent a metric as {key, kind}.
- dashboard expected {metricKey, type}.
- The parse failed, dashboard read the failure as “source is down”, and served an empty catalog with 200 OK.

With one crate, a renamed field breaks the build of every reader at the same time. A runtime surprise becomes a compile error.

The rule. The producer builds the Rust struct and serialises it. Nobody writes a shared message by hand with json!.

-----

What is inside

lib.rstelemetry.rsalerts.rsModuleMetric catalog: ServiceMetricsContract, MetricContract, MetricsDiscoveryResponseTick: TelemetryEnvelope, TelemetryReading; channel namesBreach: AlertEvent, BoundDirection; topic names; ALERTABLE_METRICSShapes and namestelemetry and digital-twin on /contractstelemetrytelemetryWritten bydashboard; frontend reads the same namesdashboard, socket, frontendnotificationRead by



Thin: Redis or HTTP. Thick: Kafka.

-----

1. The tick

Shape

One building tick is one message, from telemetry to the browser.

	{"buildingId":"b1","ingestedAt":1700000000500,
	 "readings":[
	   {"type":"temperature","roomId":"r1","timestamp":1700000000000,"value":21.5},
	   {"type":"airQuality","roomId":"r2","timestamp":1700000000000,"value":42.0,"indoorAqi":42.0,"co2":810}
	 ]}

buildingIdingestedAtreadingstyperoomIdtimestampvalueanything elseFieldenvelopeenvelopeenvelopereadingreadingreadingreadingreadingWherebuilding_idingested_at_msreadings: Vec<Value>metricroom_idts_msvalue: f64fieldsRust nameRequiredRequired. Milliseconds since 1970, set when telemetry accepted the batchRequiredRequired. The metric nameRequiredRequired. When the sensor measuredRequired. An integer like 20 reads as 20.0Kept as is, whatever the plugin put thereRule

- The envelope has no type. Only its readings do. A reader that treats a whole tick as one reading finds no type and drops every update.
- A reading never repeats buildingId: the envelope says it once. The JSON schema refuses a reading that carries it.

Why readings stay loose on the envelope

readings is a list of plain JSON values, not of TelemetryReading.

- telemetry is a microkernel: each metric is a plugin, and each plugin adds its own fields (indoorAqi, co2, pm25).
- Listing those fields here would make every new plugin edit a shared crate.
- So the crate types only the four names every reading has. #[serde(flatten)] collects the rest into fields, and writes them back unchanged.

Example. An air quality reading with indoorAqi: 42.0 and pm25: 9.5 parses into TelemetryReading, with both in fields. Serialised again, it gives the same JSON back. The test a_plugins_own_fields_ride_alongside_and_survive_a_round_trip checks exactly this.

A tick end to end

Every call a tick goes through, from the sensor batch to the browser. Names are the real functions.



What the data looks like at each step

Example: building b1, one temperature reading of 21.5 °C in room r1.

12457101314StepSensor gatewayTelemetryEvent in telemetryTelemetryReadingText on telemetry:rawTelemetryEnvelope in dashboardText on telemetry:filtered:b1Delivery in socketBrowserHolder{"buildingId":"b1","readings":[{"type":"temperature","roomId":"r1","timestamp":1700000000000,"value":21.5,"temperature":21.5}]}building b1, room r1, metric temperature, ts_ms 1700000000000, value 21.5, payload with buildingId, roomId, timestamp, temperature, ingested at 1700000000500{"type":"temperature","roomId":"r1","timestamp":1700000000000,"value":21.5,"temperature":21.5}: buildingId, roomId, timestamp taken out of the payload, so none appears twice{"buildingId":"b1","ingestedAt":1700000000500,"readings":[…step 4…]}building_id b1, ingested_at_ms 1700000000500, readings one JSON value, plus the original text kept asideIdentical to step 5, byte for byteroom building:b1, payload the parsed JSONevent telemetry, same JSON; the page picks the readings of the room it showsData

Fan-out latency for this tick: dashboard reads the clock right after step 10, say 1700000000512, and records 12 ms.

How telemetry builds a tick

adapters/driven/redis_fanout.rs, after a batch is stored:

1. No events in the batch: publish nothing and stop.
2. Take buildingId and ingestedAt from the first event. Every event of one batch has the same building: the ingest check refuses a reading that names another one.
3. For each event, build a TelemetryReading:
	- type, roomId, timestamp, value from the event;
	- fields = the plugin payload minus buildingId, roomId and timestamp, so nothing is sent twice.
4. Put the readings in one TelemetryEnvelope and serialise it.
5. Publish it on RAW_CHANNEL (telemetry:raw).
6. A failed publish is logged and counted, never returned as an error. The readings are already stored, so the batch stays accepted.

How dashboard routes a tick

dashboard/src/tunnel.rs, for every message on telemetry:raw:

1. Parse the text as a TelemetryEnvelope. Fails? Log “not a tick envelope” and skip it.
2. Hand it to a new task, so a slow publish never holds up the next message.
3. Building has no column preferences? Drop the tick.
4. Otherwise publish the original text, not a re-serialised copy, on envelope.channel(), that is telemetry:filtered:{buildingId}.
5. Record the time from ingestedAt to now as fan-out latency.



Why the original text: routing only needs buildingId. Rebuilding the JSON would make dashboard responsible for fields it does not own, and one wrong change there would silently drop them.

Channel names

RAW_CHANNELFILTERED_CHANNEL_PREFIXFILTERED_CHANNEL_PATTERNfiltered_channel(id)building_of_filtered_channel(ch)Nametelemetry:rawtelemetry:filtered:telemetry:filtered:*prefix + idch minus the prefixValuetelemetry publishes, dashboard subscribesBase of the two functions belowsocket subscribes to all buildings at oncedashboard, through envelope.channel()socket, to find which browser room gets the tickUsed by

The prefix works in both directions: dashboard writes it, socket takes it off. So the two functions must be exact opposites.

Example. Building id site:b1 contains a colon.

1. filtered_channel("site:b1") gives telemetry:filtered:site:b1.
2. building_of_filtered_channel removes only the prefix at the start, and gives site:b1 back.
3. Splitting on the last colon instead would give b1, the wrong building. The test a_building_round_trips_through_its_own_channel_name covers both b1 and site:b1.

A channel without the prefix comes back unchanged: notifications gives notifications.

-----

2. The breach

Shape

	{"buildingId":"b1","roomId":"r1","buildingName":"HQ","roomName":"Lab 2",
	 "co2":1200.0,"type":"airQuality","field":"co2","label":"CO2","unit":"ppm",
	 "direction":"high","threshold":1000.0,"timestamp":1700000000000}

buildingId, roomIdbuildingName, roomNametypefieldthe field’s own name, here co2label, unitdirectionthresholdtimestampFieldWhere it happened. These are the keysDisplay names from the building’s registrationThe metricThe payload field whose limit brokeThe value that broke itText for a person to read. unit absent when there is none, like AQIhigh (over the limit) or low (under it)The limit itselfWhen the sensor measuredMeaningErrorUses the idErrorUses typeErrorlabel uses type; unit stays emptyErrorErrorErrorIf missing when parsing

A breach end to end



- accept raises the breaches first, then calls publish_telemetry. So steps 1 to 7 happen before the tick reaches Redis.
- Step 7 only queues the message. A spawned task waits for Kafka’s answer and counts it as ok, error or cancelled. A slow broker never slows down a sensor batch.

Why the value sits under the field’s name

One metric can have limits on several fields. Air quality has limits on co2 and on indoor_aqi. So type: airQuality cannot say which one broke: field says it, and the value sits under that key.

A normal serde derive cannot read “the key that another field names”. So Serialize and Deserialize are written by hand.

How parsing works, step by step

AlertEventVisitor::visit_map reads the JSON object once, key by key:

1. A known key (buildingId, type, field, …) is stored in its own slot.
2. Any other key is kept aside as a candidate, with its value. One of these is the breaching value, but its name is not known yet.
3. After the last key, type, buildingId and roomId must exist, or parsing fails with “missing field”.
4. Missing names fall back: buildingName to the building id, roomName to the room id.
5. A missing field becomes type; a missing label also becomes type.
6. Look for the candidate named like field. It must exist and be a number. Otherwise parsing fails with alert carries no numeric "co2" value.
7. direction, threshold and timestamp must exist, or parsing fails.



Example. A message has "type":"airQuality","field":"co2" but carries the value under "airQuality": 1200.

- Step 2 keeps airQuality: 1200 as a candidate.
- Step 6 looks for co2, finds nothing, and fails.
- Result: notification parks the message on alerts.dlq. No half-filled push reaches a person.

Example, older message. {"type":"temperature","temperature":40.0,…} with no field, label or names.

- field and label become temperature; the names become b1 and r1.
- Step 6 finds temperature: 40.0. The message parses.

The fallbacks exist for messages written before those fields existed. They still sit on the Kafka topic and can be read again.

How writing works

Serialize writes the keys in a fixed order: ids, names, <field>: value, type, field, label, unit only when present, direction, threshold, timestamp. The value is written under field’s name, so a CO₂ breach has a co2 key and no airQuality key.

Helpers

partition_key()BoundDirection::wire_name()is_alertable()ALERTS_TOPICALERTS_DLQ_TOPICItem"{buildingId}:{roomId}", like b1:r1high or lowtrue when type is in ALERTABLE_METRICSalertsalerts.dlqGivestelemetry uses it as the Kafka key. Kafka keeps messages with one key in order, so one room’s breaches arrive in the order they happenedThe same text serde writes, used as a metrics label in telemetry. A test checks the two agreenotification drops and counts any other metricTopic for every breachWhere notification parks a message it cannot useWhy

ALERTABLE_METRICS

temperature, airQuality, peopleCount: the metrics notification can deliver.

- telemetry has a test that compares this list to the plugins that declare limits. A new plugin with limits fails that test until it joins the list.
- notification uses the same list as the alert types a person can switch on or off. There is no second copy.

Example. A humidity plugin gets limits. every_plugin_with_bounds_is_alertable_and_nothing_else_is in telemetry/src/plugins.rs fails. After humidity joins the list, notification delivers it and offers it as a choice, with no change in notification.

-----

3. The metric catalog

Shape

GET /contracts on telemetry and on digital-twin answers a ServiceMetricsContract:

	{"service":"telemetry","metrics":[
	  {"kind":"temperature","label":"Temperature","interface":"ITemperature","unit":"°C",
	   "fields":[{"name":"temperature","type":"Finite","required":true}],
	   "actions":[{"name":"setTarget","label":"Set target temperature",
	               "parameters":[{"name":"target","type":"Finite","required":true}]}]}
	]}

ServiceMetricsContractMetricContractMetricFieldContractActionContractActionParameterContractStructservice, metricskind, label, interface, unit, fields, actions, sourcename, type, required, descriptionname, label, parametersname, type, requiredFieldsunit always written, null when none. actions may be missing on read, then empty. source left out when emptydescription left out when emptyA command a device acceptsRules

A catalog request end to end



push_unique_metric skips a metric when one already in the list has the same kind, interface and source. The same kind from two sources stays twice, once per source.

Example. telemetry answers temperature, airQuality, peopleCount; digital-twin times out after 2 s. The browser gets 3 metrics after about 2 s, and dashboard logs Failed to reach …. The answer is still 200.

How dashboard reads a catalog

dashboard/src/api/dashboard.rs, for each source found in *_METRICS_URL:

1. Call it, with a 2 s timeout. No answer: log it, use an empty list.
2. Parse the body as MetricsDiscoveryResponse. It accepts two forms:
	- an object {service, metrics}, the form telemetry and digital-twin send;
	- a bare list of metrics.
3. Each metric with no source gets one: the service from the body, or the source name from the env var.
4. Parse fails: log it, use an empty list.

MetricsDiscoveryResponse is untagged: serde tries each form in turn and takes the first that fits. When neither fits, the only sign is the log line in step 4. That is why the producer must build from these same structs.

-----

4. Shapes checked by fixture only

Some telemetry messages have no Rust type here: one side is Python or TypeScript, or the only Rust side reads raw JSON. Each still has a fixture and a JSON schema, and this crate runs the check because it already depends on jsonschema.

ingest-batch.jsonsimulation-start.jsoncollector-routers.jsonconnected-devices.jsonFixturesimulators, devices → telemetry POST /ingesttelemetry → simulators POST /control/starttelemetry → collector GET /collectortelemetry → browser GET /connected-devices/buildings/{id}From → to{buildingId, readings[]}, at most 500 readings{buildingId, sensors: [{sensorId, sensorType, roomId}]}The routers to pollThe building’s device totalBody

Rules of simulation-start:

- sensors replaces what the simulator holds for the building. An empty list means stop.
- roomId is always a room: readings are keyed by room, so outdoor sensors are never sent.
- No positions: those belong to digital-twin.
- No target URL: a simulator posts to its own TELEMETRY_INGEST_URL, so a caller cannot redirect signed readings. The schema refuses extra keys.

-----

Tests

Three layers, each catching a different mistake:

Rust typesFixturesJSON schemasLayerA Rust reader and writer that disagree: the build failsOne language parsing a message differently from anotherA fixture drifting from the written contractCatchesEvery service depends on this cratetests/*_conformance.rs here; the same JSON files in the other languages’ teststests/*_schema.rsWhere

What the tests here pin down:

src/telemetry.rssrc/alerts.rssrc/lib.rstelemetry_envelope_conformance.rsmetric_contract_conformance.rs*_schema.rsTest fileWire names; plugin fields survive; 20 reads as 20.0; no envelope without buildingId or readings; channel round tripValue keyed by field; unit left out when empty; old messages parse; wrong key fails and names the field; every required field required; b1:r1 keySingle-word names; actions optional on read; both catalog formsEvery fixture tick re-serialises byte for byte; every rejected tick failsThe fixture parses, re-serialises byte for byte, keeps "unit": nullAccepted cases pass, rejected cases fail, plus the 500-reading cap and old field names refusedChecks

On the other side, telemetry/src/adapters/driven/redis_fanout.rs must publish each fixture tick byte for byte, and the frontend’s src/utils/commons/telemetry.ts spec replays the same file.

	mise exec -- cargo test --manifest-path schemas/telemetry-schema/Cargo.toml

-----

Changing a shape

Use the contract skill. In short, in one change:

1. Edit the struct here.
2. Edit the fixture and the JSON schema.
3. Fix every service that no longer builds.
4. Update the other languages’ readers, which the fixture tests now fail.

-----

Building a service that uses it

The dependency is a path on disk, ../../schemas/telemetry-schema. So:

- each consumer’s image builds from the repo root (cd_context: "." in .github/services.json);
- each Dockerfile copies the crate before cargo chef prepare and before each cargo chef cook. cook reads the dependency graph again; a path missing at that moment fails the build half way.

entries.title: Notification Schema
entries.content:
Notification Schema

CrateNotificationBellWeb PushService workerSeverityDomainRoom (socket)FixtureWordA Rust library other Rust code builds againstOne message to people of one domainThe in-app list of messages in the browserA pop-up the browser shows even with the page closedA browser script that receives Web PushHow serious a message is: info, warning, dangerA group of people and buildings inside an organizationA named group of browser connectionsA JSON file of example messages every language must agree onMeaningnotification-schema“Lab 2 Temperature is 31.4 °C”Top bar iconSent through the browser maker’s push serverfrontend/public/service-worker.jsdanger for a breachengdomain:engschemas/fixtures/notification.jsonExample

Rust crate at schemas/notification-schema. It holds the one message notification sends to people, and the Redis channel it travels on.

Depends only on serde and serde_json. Tests also use jsonschema.

-----

Why one shape for two deliveries

notification delivers every message twice:

- to the bell, through Redis and socket;
- as a Web Push pop-up, through the browser’s push server.

Both get the same Notification value, serialised by the same code. So the bell and the pop-up can never show different text for one event.



-----

What is inside

NOTIFICATIONS_CHANNELSeverityNotificationItemnotificationsinfo, warning, dangerThe messageValuenotification publishes, socket subscribesField type; FromStr parses the text of POST /notification/triggernotification builds, socket parses, browser readsUsed by

-----

The message

	{"id":"1757251200000","type":"danger",
	 "title":"Temperature Alert - Innovation Hub",
	 "message":"Innovation Hub : Lab 2 Temperature is 31.4 °C (above maximum)",
	 "timestamp":"2025-09-07T13:20:00.000Z","domainName":"eng","metric":"temperature"}

idtypetitlemessagetimestampdomainNamemetriciconFieldid: Stringr#type: Severitytitlemessagetimestamp: Stringdomain_nameOption<String>Option<String>RustMillisecond clock at build time, as textOnly info, warning, danger. Anything else fails to parseRequiredRequiredISO-8601 in UTC with milliseconds, never a numberRequired and not emptySet on a breach only. Left out when emptyLeft out when emptyRuleBell, to tell items apartBell colourPop-up headingBell text and pop-up bodyBellsocket, to pick the roomBell filterService workerRead by

- type is the severity, not the metric. The metric sits in metric.
- domainName has its own check, non_empty. A plain String would accept "", and "" names no room.

Why a missing domain must fail

socket routes by domainName and never broadcasts. If a message with no domain parsed, socket would have no room for it. The safe outcome is “not a notification”: it is skipped.

Example. {"type":"danger",…,"domainName":""}

1. socket calls serde_json::from_str::<Notification>.
2. non_empty sees "" and returns must not be empty.
3. get_notification_delivery_plan returns None. socket counts it as skipped. No browser gets it.

-----

A breach notification end to end



Data at each step

Example: a 31.4 °C breach in Lab 2 of Innovation Hub, building owned by domain eng, clock at 1757251200000.

1345810121315Stepon_breachargumentsNotificationText on notificationsDelivery in socketBellAccountsPush bodyPop-upHolder["eng"]id and time 1757251200000, Danger, title Temperature Alert - Innovation Hub, message Innovation Hub : Lab 2 Temperature is 31.4 °C (above maximum), domain engthe JSON above; timestamp from iso8601(1757251200000) is 2025-09-07T13:20:00.000Zthe same JSON as one stringroom domain:eng, payload the parsed JSONshown only if preferences["eng"]["temperature"] === truee.g. ["ada"]: only accounts that switched temperature on for engthe same JSON as bytes, then encrypted with the subscription’s keysheading Temperature Alert - Innovation Hub, body the message, no iconData

What the bell decides

frontend/src/utils/commons/notification.ts, isVisible:



Push makes the same choice on the server, in accounts_subscribed_to. So one rule, applied in two places.

-----

A manual notification

POST /notification/trigger builds the same shape, through Alerts::trigger:

1. Empty message? Use Manual Alert Triggered.
2. type given? Parse it with Severity::from_str. alert or any other word gives 400 type must be one of: info, warning, danger. No type: danger.
3. buildingName missing: 400.
4. Find the domains of the building, then keep only the ones the caller may reach.
5. One notification per kept domain, title CrowdVision Alert, no metric. So the bell always shows it.

Example. {"message":"Fire drill at 15:00","type":"warning","buildingName":"Innovation Hub"} from a member of eng gives one warning to room domain:eng.

-----

Tests

tests/notification_conformance.rstests/notification_schema.rstests/notification_preferences_schema.rsnotification domain/notification.rssocket core/relay.rsfrontend notification.spec.tsWhereEvery fixture case re-serialises byte for byte; every rejected case fails; Severity parses only its own names; channel is notificationsEvery fixture case passes schemas/json/notification.schema.json; every rejected case fails itThe GET / POST /notification/preferences fixture against its schemaid is the clock as text; timestamp like 2023-11-14T22:13:20.123Z; type not kind; no icon by defaultEvery case routed to its domain room, every rejection skippedEvery severity has a colour; isVisible follows the stored preferencesChecks

Rejected cases in the fixture: no domainName, empty domainName, type: "alert", no title, a number as timestamp.

The preferences fixture has no Rust type here: only notification parses it, and it reads raw JSON. The crate hosts the schema check because it already depends on jsonschema.

	mise exec -- cargo test --manifest-path schemas/notification-schema/Cargo.toml

Auth Middleware
