entries.title: Testing Tools
entries.content:
Testing Tools

Unit testIntegration testThrowaway stackFixtureFitness testBuild tagtestcontainersE2EEvalCoverageWordChecks one piece of code alone, with no database or brokerChecks code against real infrastructureContainers started for one test run, then deleted with their dataA JSON file of example messages that every language must parse the same wayA test that checks which folder may import whichA Go switch that includes some files only when askedA Go library that starts a container from inside a testA browser test that drives the real appA scored run of the assistant against fixed questionsThe share of code lines a test run went throughMeaningA threshold check with fake storestelemetry writing to a real TimescaleDBProject telemetry-integration-testsschemas/fixtures/telemetry-envelope.jsontelemetry/tests/architecture.rs//go:build integrationA real Postgres for tenancyPlaywright opens the twin viewevals/dataset.json78 % of telemetryExample

Every service has fast unit tests that need nothing running, and slower tests that need real infrastructure. They are kept apart, so just test all runs green on a laptop with nothing started.

-----

The test layers

UnitFitnessConformanceIntegration, per serviceAcceptance, across servicesBrowser E2EAgent evalsLayernothingnothingthe shared fixturesDockerDockera dev server, Chromiumthe running stack, an LLM keyNeedsjust test <svc>, just test all, just test affectedpart of the Rust unit runpart of the unit run, or of the integration run for Rust tests/*.rsjust test <svc>-integrationjust test integrationjust test frontend-e2ejust test evalRuns withevery PR, per serviceevery PRevery PRRust and Go templatesci-acceptance.ymlnot runnot runIn CI

-----

Unit tests, per language

RustGoPythonTypeScript, frontendTypeScript, NodeLanguagecargo testgo testpytestVitestJestRunnercargo test --lib, plus --test architecture or --test architecture_fitness where one existsgo test ./...npm test for agent, uv run pytest elsewherenpm run test:unit = vitest runnpm testmoon task commandsrc/ holds only unit tests; tests/*.rs needs infraFiles with //go:build integration are left outagent adds --cov=app; asyncio_mode = "auto"happy-dom, threads; only src/utils/** logicsensor-simulatorNotes

telemetry, socketchat, notificationdigital-twin, dashboardServicecargo test --lib --test architecturecargo test --lib --test architecture_fitnesscargo test --libUnit command

- Every inherited test task lists /schemas/fixtures/** and /schemas/json/** as inputs. Without them, editing a fixture would replay a cached pass.
- Frontend unit tests cover pure logic only. Components and views are covered by E2E and the acceptance suite.

-----

Fitness tests

A Rust test reads the source files and fails when a layer imports one it must not.

telemetrysocketchat, digital-twin, notificationServicetests/architecture.rstests/architecture.rstests/architecture_fitness.rsFiletypes, kernel, plugins, adapterscore, shell, main.rsdomain, service, adapters/driving, adapters/drivenLayers

Example. A line use sqlx::PgPool; in telemetry/src/kernel/ingest.rs fails telemetry:test: sqlx is an IO crate the kernel may not name.

-----

Conformance across languages

One fixture, read by each language’s own parser. A rename that one language misses fails that language’s test.



standard-claims.jsoninternal-signature.jsonauth-policy casestelemetry-envelope.jsonbuilding.jsoningest-batch.json, simulation-start.jsonFixtureclaims-schema, auth-contracts/conformance_test.go, agent test_claims_conformance.pyauth-contracts/internalsig_test.go, telemetry ingest checkauth-policy/conformance_test.go, digital-twin and telemetry tests/cedar_conformance.rs, agent test_cedar_conformance.pytelemetry-schema, telemetry fan-out, frontend telemetry.spec.tsdigital-twin tests/building_conformance.rs, frontend building.spec.tstelemetry, aq-simulator, ap-simulator, sensor-simulatorRead by

Trap. A Rust conformance test in tests/ is an integration test target. telemetry:test runs only --lib --test architecture, so tests/cedar_conformance.rs runs with just test telemetry-integration and in CI, not with just test telemetry.

-----

Integration, Rust: a throwaway compose stack

just test telemetry-integration, end to end



234578912Stepcache: false: a pass that depends on Docker must never be replayedThe base image’s compiler is the one pinA trap, not a last line: under set -e a failed up would skip a trailing down--abort-on-container-exit stops all once the test container endsSame images as productionTest env points at container names, never at host portsOne --test per file, so unit tests do not run again--volumes deletes the data: the next run starts emptyWhat happensRUST_VERSION=1.99.1timescale/timescaledb:2.30.0-pg17, redis:8.10.1-alpine, apache/kafka:4.3.1DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:telemetry@telemetry-db:5432/telemetrydbcargo test --test alerts --test api --test architecture …Real value

The same scripts/test/rust-integration-tests.sh runs in CI. There, tpl-rust-ci.yml starts the infra as job services on localhost, sets MONGO_URI, REDIS_URL, DATABASE_URL, KAFKA_BROKERS, and passes --release.

telemetrydigital-twin, chatnotification, dashboardsocketServiceTimescaleDB, Redis, KafkaMongoDBMongoDB, RedisRedisThrowaway infra

-----

Integration, Go: testcontainers

registry and tenancy keep their Postgres tests in files tagged //go:build integration.



- just test tenancy-integration runs go test -tags=integration -count 1 ./....
- -count 1 turns off Go’s own test cache. moon’s cache: false alone still lets Go replay an old pass, which proves nothing when the real dependency is a running Docker daemon.
- The command is written as command plus args. Packed into one string, moon dropped the tag, the suite printed [no test files], and the task still exited 0.
- CI runs go test -tags=integration ./... on every Go module.

-----

Acceptance: across services

just test integration runs backend/acceptance/run-integration-tests.sh.

1. Generate the ingest keys into .env, so the suite runs without just stack env.
2. Read RUST_VERSION from .mise.toml.
3. Write compose.integration-tests.runtime.yml, which include:s only what the suite touches: rust-base, the suite’s Redis and Kafka, telemetry, socket, dashboard, and the test runner.
4. Remove a stopped leftover crowd-vision-socket, never a running one: it may belong to just stack dev.
5. up --build --exit-code-from integration-tests, under project crowdvision-integration-tests, so it never collides with the dev stack.
6. down --remove-orphans --volumes, then exit with the tests’ code.

include: rather than several -f flags: each fragment’s relative build.context must resolve from its own folder, and chained -f does not do that reliably.

edge/dashboard_freshness/metrics_catalog/sensor_registry/wireless/FolderRouting at the edgeLive update, reconnect catch-up, sustained throughput, latencyThe merged catalogSensor writesThe collector contractCovers

-----

Browser E2E: Playwright

just test frontend-e2e, end to end



2467StepLocally the dev server; with CI set, npm run preview on port 4173No backend runs. Each spec answers the API itselfTimeoutsSpecs collect pageerror and fail on anyWhat happensreuseExistingServer only off CI/tenancy/me/memberships returns [{domain:"eng",role:"business_admin"}]30 s per test, 5 s per expectsensors-mode.spec.tsReal value

- Only Chromium: the twin needs WebGPU or WebGL2, and Chromium is what it is built against. Run npx playwright install chromium once.
- Headed locally, headless on CI. On CI: 2 retries, 1 worker, a trace on the first retry.
- Specs: camera, connected-devices, devices-mode, sensors-mode, sensors, simulator.

Gap. No workflow runs these specs. ci-frontend.yml runs lint, type check, audit and Vitest only.

-----

Agent evals

just test eval models=… judge=… runs backend/agent/evals/run_evals.py --report-only against the local stack.

1. Read evals/dataset.json: one question per row, with what the answer must contain.
2. Mint an HS256 eval token, sub evalbot, signed with EVAL_JWT_SECRET from the environment or the repo-root .env. No sign-in is needed; a remote agent needs AUTH_COOKIE instead.
3. Check once that the agent answers, and stop with a clear error if not.
4. Ask every row; score it on the expected content.
5. Rows with llm_judge are also graded by a judge model. They need JUDGE_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY or LLM_API_KEY.
6. A row marked xfail must say why. With --report-only the run reports and exits 0.

just test agent-integration is a separate pytest tests/integration suite.

-----

Coverage

Published from master by cd-coverage.yml, only for services that changed.

RustGoPythonTypeScriptLanguagecargo llvm-cov --all-targets, then cargo llvm-cov report --lcovgo test -tags=integration -coverpkg=./... -coverprofile=coverage.outpytest --covVitest v8 providerToolcoverage/coverage-summary.json, coverage/lcov.infocoverage.out, turned into coverage.xmlcoverage.xmlcoverage/coverage-summary.json, coverage/lcov.infoOutput

1. Each changed service uploads its numbers and its line-level report.
2. The previous coverage-counts.json and reports/ come from branch coverage-data, so unchanged services keep their last numbers and their last report.
3. scripts/coverage-summary.py merges them into badge.json and summary.json, and writes reports/<service>.json: per file, the lines and branches covered and the ranges of lines no test runs.
4. The files are force-pushed as one commit to coverage-data. The push is tried 3 times, 10 s and 20 s apart.
5. The Test Coverage page of this site fetches summary.json and coverage-counts.json from that branch in the browser, and a service’s reports/<service>.json when its row is clicked.

Example, real numbers from ap-collector. pytest reports app/probes.py with 8 of 145 lines missed: 64, 146, 172-177, 209. reports/ap-collector.json holds the same file as "lines_covered": 137, "lines_total": 145, "uncovered": [[64,64],[146,146],[172,177],[209,209]], and the page shows it first, as 94.5% with links L64, L146, L172–177, L209.

-----

All just test recipes

just test alljust test affectedjust test <svc>just test <svc>-integrationjust test frontend-e2ejust test agent-integrationjust test evaljust test integrationRecipemoon run :test, every projectmoon run :test --affectedUnit tests of one project: chat, telemetry, twin, notification, dashboard, socket, claims-gateway, provisioner, registry, tenancy, frontend, agent, ap-collector, ap-simulator, aq-simulator, sensor-simulatorchat, telemetry, twin, notification, dashboard, socket, registry, tenancyPlaywrightAgent pytest tests/integrationAgent evalsThe acceptance suiteRuns

Trap. The tenancy-integration recipe says it also covers “the account-deleted consumer”. No such consumer exists in tenancy.

See also: Build System, Docker Compose, CI.

entries.title: Docker Images
entries.content:
Docker Images

ImageStageTargetBuild contextNamed contextLayer cachecargo-chefRecipeDistrolesssccacheTrivyWordA frozen file system plus a start command, ready to run as a containerOne FROM block of a Dockerfile. Later stages copy files out of earlier onesThe stage a build stops atThe folder whose files a Dockerfile may COPYAn extra build context, given a name a FROM can useDocker reuses a step when its inputs did not changeA tool that splits “build the dependencies” from “build the service”The dependency list cargo-chef writes, with no source codeA base image with no shell and no package managerA compiler cache that keeps compiled crates between buildsA scanner that fails the build on known holes in OS packagesMeaningcrowdvision-telemetryplanner, builder, productiontarget: dev in composeThe repo root, .rust-baseA cook skipped because recipe.json is the sameprepare, then cookrecipe.jsongcr.io/distroless/cc-debian12:nonroot/sccache cache mountRun in ci-docker and cd-registryExample

Every deployable part ships as one image. Each service keeps its Dockerfile beside its code, and all images follow one of five patterns, one per language. The images are built in three places: by Compose on a laptop, by ci-docker on a pull request, and by cd-registry on master.

-----

The images

telemetry, digital-twin, notification, socket, dashboard, chatclaims-gateway, tenancy, registry, provisioneragentaq-simulator, ap-simulator, ap-collectorfrontendsensor-simulatorPartRustGoPython, two stagesPython, one stageStatic siteNodePatternbackend/<svc>/Dockerfilebackend/<svc>/Dockerfilebackend/agent/Dockerfile<dir>/Dockerfilefrontend/Dockerfilesimulators/sensor-simulator/DockerfileDockerfilerepo rootrepo rootrepo rootown folderfrontend/own folderBuild contextgcr.io/distroless/cc-debian12:nonrootgcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonrootpython:3.14.8-slimpython:3.14.8-slimnginx:1.31.5-alpinenode:24.21.0-alpineProduction base300030003000300080803000Port

Why the repo root is the context for most of them: a service reads files that live outside its own folder.

Rust servicestelemetry, digital-twinGo servicesagentServiceschemas/*-schemabackend/libs/auth-policy, backend/libs/auth-contractsbackend/libs/*backend/libs/auth-policy, backend/libs/auth-contractsReads from outside its folderPath dependencies in Cargo.toml, like telemetry-schema = { path = "../../schemas/telemetry-schema" }The Cedar bundle and roles.json, read when compilingGo modules replaced by local pathsapp/cedar_authz.py reads the policy files at run time, by a path relative to itselfWhy

A Docker build cannot COPY anything above its context. So a context of backend/telemetry could never reach schemas/.

-----

.github/services.json

One file lists every package. CI reads it to know what to build and how.

keydirlangimagecd_contextdockerfilebuilds_binarydepends_onneeds_mongo, needs_redis, needs_kafka, needs_postgresciFieldShort name; also the CI artifact name binary-<key>Where the code livesPicks the CI template and the Docker patternImage name on GHCRBuild context for cd-registry. . is the repo root; missing means dirDockerfile path, from the repo rootfalse for a library: nothing to put in an imageFolders it builds or tests from; a change there rebuilds its image tooWhich databases CI starts for the integration testsfalse keeps a package out of the CI gateMeaningtwinbackend/digital-twinrust, go, python, node, frontendcrowdvision-twin.backend/digital-twin/Dockerfileauth-policytwin: schemas/twin-schematelemetry: Redis, Postgres, Kafkathe three simulatorsExample

Two names break the “one name everywhere” rule here: digital-twin has key twin and image crowdvision-twin; sensor-simulator has image crowdvision-simulator.

-----

Rust: one Dockerfile, five stages

All six Rust Dockerfiles have the same shape. telemetry is the example.



plannerdevtestbuilderproductionStagethe two belowjust stack dev (target: dev) and docker-compose.test.ymlchat, socket, notification onlyproductioncd-registry, just k8s build, just stack startUsed byrecipe.jsonA ready debug build and cargo watch -x runDebug dependencies and the source, no build: integration tests compile once and exitThe release binaryThe image that runsResult

A release build, step by step



12–3456789–1011–13StepStart from the shared toolchainPut the service and its schema crates where ../../schemas/... pointsWrite recipe.json: every dependency and its version, no source codeOnly the recipe enters builder, not the sourceThe schema crates go in again: they are path dependencies, and cargo needs them on disk to cookCompile every dependency: tokio, axum, sqlx, rdkafka…Files read only by the service’s own code, like policy.cedar, come after the cookCompile the service itselfCopy only the binary and libz.so.1, which distroless lacksWhat happensrust-base unchanged——recipe.json byte-identicalschema files unchangedSteps 5–6 unchanged: a source edit keeps this layer—Never, after a source change—Cached when

Example. A one-line change in src/kernel/ingest.rs:

- recipe.json comes out the same, so step 7 is cached.
- Only steps 9–10 run: one crate compiles instead of a few hundred.

Why the schemas are copied before each cook, not only before prepare. Each stage starts from chef, with an empty /app/schemas. prepare needs the crates to read their Cargo.toml. cook needs them again to build them. A crate missing at cook time stops the build half way, with cargo failing to read /app/schemas/<crate>/Cargo.toml.

The debug stage and sccache

dev, and debug-deps where it exists, cooks under sccache:

	RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/sccache,sharing=shared \
	    RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache SCCACHE_DIR=/sccache CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 \
	    cargo chef cook --recipe-path recipe.json

- The wrapper is set on that one step, so it never reaches the release stages or the running container.
- It helps when the cook must run again but the cache is warm: a Cargo.toml change, or a schema change. Then most crates come from /sccache.
- It does not help a first build: the cache is empty, and sccache adds its own hashing on top.
- sharing=shared is safe: entries are keyed by a hash of the compiler inputs and written whole.

Then dev runs a plain cargo build, with the same flags cargo run uses. A container then starts with nothing left to compile.

docker/rust-base

A build-only image every Rust Dockerfile starts from.

rust:${RUST_VERSION}-bookwormmold, build-essentialcargo-chef 0.1.78, cargo-watch 8.5.3, sccache 0.17.0RUSTFLAGS="-C link-arg=-fuse-ld=mold"HoldsRUST_VERSION comes from the one pin in .mise.tomlmold links faster; a C compiler is needed because rdkafka-sys compiles librdkafkaPrebuilt releases, each checked against a SHA-256 for amd64 and arm64. Compiling them in every image cost far more than downloadingEvery stage that starts from it links with moldWhy

How each builder finds it:

Composecd-registryIntegration runnersWherebuild.additional_contexts: rust-base: service:rust-base. docker/rust-base/docker-compose.yml declares it with scale: 0, so it is built but never runbuild-contexts: rust-base=docker-image://ghcr.io/<owner>/crowdvision-rust-base:<rust>-<hash>. The hash is the first 12 characters of the Dockerfile’s SHA-256, so an unchanged base is never rebuiltInclude docker/rust-base/docker-compose.yml and export RUST_VERSION themselvesHow FROM rust-base resolves

-----

Go: four identical stages

	tools  ->  base  ->  dev        (air, live reload)
	              \->  builder  ->  production

toolsbasedevbuilderproductionStageDownloads air 1.67.1, checks its SHA-256. The text is identical in all four Dockerfiles, so BuildKit builds it onceCopies the backend/libs/* modules the service uses, then the service, at their real repo paths. tenancy: all three. registry, provisioner: auth-contractsCopies air out of tools; runs air -c .air.tomlCGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /out/<svc> ./cmd/<svc>: a static binary, no C library neededdistroless/static-debian12:nonroot, the binary, and for tenancy and registry the migrations/ folderWhat it does

The libraries keep their real paths because each service’s go.mod replaces them with ../libs/....

-----

Python

agentaq-simulator, ap-simulatorap-collectorImagebuilder, productiononeoneStagesuv pip install --system --prefix /install ., then the folder is copied into /usr/localuv sync --locked --no-dev: exactly what uv.lock says—How dependencies are installedalembic upgrade head && uvicorn app.main:appuvicorn api:apppython -m app --config collector.json --dry-runStart command

- agent runs its database migrations on every start, before serving.
- agent copies backend/libs/auth-policy and auth-contracts to /app/backend/libs/, the same place relative to app/ as in the repo.
- Each slim image runs apt-get upgrade first, so the Trivy gate sees patched OS packages.

-----

Node and the frontend

frontendsensor-simulatorImagebuild-stage: npm ci, npm run build with VITE_SERVER_URL, VITE_KEYCLOAK_URL. production-stage: nginx serves dist/builder: build dist/. production: npm ci --omit=dev and dist/StagesVITE_* values are baked in at build time: one image per URLWorks in /repo/simulators/sensor-simulator, two levels deep, because the lockfile links ../../tooling/eslint-config. At /app the link would point above the file system root and npm ci refuses the lockfileNotes

nginx serves the frontend because a static site needs no Node: about 64 MB against 167 MB, and it starts at once.

-----

User, health and size

Who runs the process

Rust, GoPython, Node, nginxImagesnonroot, uid 65532, from the distroless tagroot: no USER lineUser

Health checks

Distroless has no shell, so no curl and no wget. Two services check themselves:

telemetry, socket productionRust dev targetsGo dev targetsagentKubernetesWhere["CMD", "/usr/local/bin/<svc>", "--health"]: the binary calls its own /health and exits 0 or 1curl -sf http://localhost:3000/health: the dev image is full Debianwget … http://localhost:3000/healthA one-line Python urllib callhttpGet /health probes; no command inside the imageCheck

start_interval: 2s checks every 2 s while a container starts, so the services that wait on it start as soon as it answers.

Size

Real sizes of the local dev images, from docker images:

crowd-vision-telemetry (dev)crowd-vision-digital-twin (dev)crowd-vision-socket (dev)crowd-vision-rust-baseEach Go service (dev)crowd-vision-agentcrowd-vision-ap-simulatorImage6.17 GB6.07 GB3.47 GB2.28 GB1.25 GB449 MB291 MBSize

A dev image holds the whole toolchain and a debug build. The production stage keeps only the binary on distroless, so it is a small fraction of that; no production size is recorded here.

-----

The images CI builds

The images on GHCR are not always built from the Dockerfiles above.



Go, RustNodePythonFrontendLanguage.github/docker/Dockerfile.ci: copies the CI binary to /app/main.github/docker/Dockerfile.node.ci: the CI dist/ plus npm ci --omit=devThe service’s own Dockerfile, with no cache, so apt-get upgrade really runsIts own Dockerfile, context frontend/ci-docker buildsalpine:3.24.3node:24.21.0-alpineas aboveas aboveBase

Why: the binary is already compiled and tested in the CI job, so the Docker job does not compile it again.

-----

Traps

- A merged pull request ships the CI image. cd-registry promotes the :pr-<sha> image when it exists, so :latest for a Go or Rust service is alpine plus the CI binary, not the distroless production stage. The CI binary is built on an Ubuntu runner: Rust links against glibc, and Go runs without CGO_ENABLED=0, while Alpine ships musl. tenancy and registry also lose their migrations/ folder. Not run here; read from the workflows.
- just k8s build names images by hand. It lists 12 docker build lines with their own paths and contexts, separate from .github/services.json. A new service must be added to both.
- A new path dependency means four COPY lines. One in planner, one before each cook (dev or debug-deps, builder). Missing one fails only that stage.
- Python and Node images run as root. kube-score’s user check is switched off in ci-k8s.
- VITE_* values are fixed at build time. Changing the backend URL needs a new frontend image, not a new environment variable.

Related: Docker Compose, Kubernetes & Istio, CI.

entries.title: Docker Compose
entries.content:
Docker Compose

Compose fileFragmentDev overrideinclude:ProjectVolumeWatchEdgeforward_authWordA YAML list of containers, their images, ports and volumesOne service’s own compose fileA second file that changes a fragment for live editingA Compose key that loads other compose files, each from its own folderThe group of containers Compose starts together, under one nameStorage that outlives the containerCompose copies changed files into a running container, or rebuilds itThe one entry point every browser request goes throughCaddy asks another service “may this request pass?” before sending it onMeaningbackend/telemetry/docker-compose.ymlbackend/chat/docker-compose.ymldocker-compose.dev.ymlcompose.runtime.ymlcrowdvision-integration-teststelemetry-datadevelop.watchCaddy on port 80claims-gateway /verifyExample

Locally the whole platform runs under Docker Compose. No single file lists every service: each service keeps its own compose file beside its code, and a small script joins them into one on every start.

-----

The files

docker-compose.yml (root)backend/<svc>/docker-compose.ymlbackend/<svc>/docker-compose.dev.ymlbackend/<svc>/docker-compose.test.ymlbackend/acceptance/docker-compose.*.ymldocker/rust-base/docker-compose.ymlsimulators/*/, devices/ap-collector/, frontend/FileShared parts only: gateway (Caddy), redis, kafka, keycloak, keycloak-db, prometheus, grafana; includes docker/rust-baseThe service and its own databaseChanges for just stack dev: target: dev, watch rules, published database ports, database browsersA throwaway stack for that service’s integration testsThe cross-service acceptance stackThe Rust build image, scale: 0Same base + dev pairHolds—telemetry, telemetry-dbtelemetry-db-guitelemetry-testintegration-testsrust-baseclientExample

- Why per service. A service is added or removed without touching a central file, and its compose file moves with it.
- No custom networks. No file declares networks:, so every container of a project joins Compose’s default network and reaches the others by service name: telemetry:3000, redis:6379.
- backend/agent holds 9 services: agent, agent-db, agent-ingester and the Langfuse stack (langfuse-web, langfuse-worker, langfuse-db, redis-langfuse, clickhouse, minio).

-----

just stack dev, step by step



23579111213Stepcreate, vapid, token, config, langfuse, keycloak, controlplane, gateway-key, ingest-key, telemetry-db, rustOnly rust.sh rewrites a value every time--no-agent becomes the substring agentEach folder adds docker-compose.yml, and in dev also docker-compose.dev.ymlOne include: entry per folder; a pair becomes one entry with two pathsA stopped container with a container_name would block up with a name clashThe root file is always included, so its services can only be dropped by nameCOMPOSE_BAKE=true: builds go through BuildKit Bake, in parallelWhat happensEach one skips a key already in .envRUST_VERSION= the pin in .mise.tomlEXCLUDE_GROUPS["agent"] = ("agent",)backend/agent skipped: printed excluded: backend/agent16 entries: root, 10 backend, 3 simulators, ap-collector, frontendcrowd-vision-socket——Real value

The generated file looks like this:

	# Auto-generated by scripts/compose/compose-run.py — do not commit.
	include:
	  - path: docker-compose.yml
	  - path:
	      - backend/chat/docker-compose.yml
	      - backend/chat/docker-compose.dev.yml
	  - path:
	      - backend/claims-gateway/docker-compose.yml
	      - backend/claims-gateway/docker-compose.dev.yml

compose.runtime.yml is in .gitignore.

Why include: and not several -f flags

With -f a.yml -f b.yml, Compose resolves every relative path against the first file’s folder. build.context: ../.. in backend/telemetry/docker-compose.yml would then point two levels above the repo root. include: resolves each file against its own folder.

A pair of files is one entry because two separate entries may not define the same service: Compose stops with a conflict.

Leaving parts out



--no-agent--no-metrics--no-simulators--no-devicesbare wordFlagagentprometheus, grafanasimulatorap-collectoritselfPatternsbackend/agent, all 9 servicesTwo root services, by nameThe three simulator foldersdevices/ap-collectorAnything whose folder or service name contains itLeaves out

Example. just stack dev chat:

1. Folder backend/chat contains chat: its two files are not included.
2. No other service name contains chat, so nothing else goes.

Example of a trap. just stack dev db drops every service with db in its name: twin-db, telemetry-db, keycloak-db… and the stack cannot start.

Modes

just stack devjust stack dev --buildjust stack startjust stack downjust stack logs <svc>--dry-runRecipedevdevstartdown—anyModeup --watch --remove-orphansthe same, plus --buildup --build -d --remove-orphans, production stages, in the backgrounddown --remove-orphans, always everythingdocker compose -f compose.runtime.yml logs -f <svc>Prints the docker command and stops after writing the fileCommand

-----

The edge: Caddy

gateway runs caddy:2.11.7 on ${BACKEND_PORT} (80), with the repo-root Caddyfile mounted read-only.

/gateway/*/tenancy/*, /twin/*, /notification/*, /chat/*, /dashboard, /dashboard/*, /telemetry/*/socket.io/*/agent/*/telemetry/ingest, /telemetry/collector, /telemetry/observations/prometheus/*, /grafana/*/<x>-db-gui/*/langfuse*Pathclaims-gateway:3000the servicesocket:3000agent:3000telemetry:3000the toolthe database browser of each Mongo service and telemetryredirect to port 3030Goes tonoyesyesno, and X-Gateway-Claims is removedno: the body is HMAC-signed and checked inside telemetrynono—Gatedyesyesno: Socket.IO expects its own pathyes/telemetry only/prometheus onlyno—Prefix removed

/chat/* adds flush_interval -1: answers stream as SSE, and buffering would deliver every token at the end.

A gated request



134810StepCookie: authentication_token=eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIs…extractToken reads Authorization: Bearer … first, then the cookieSignature checked against claims-gateway’s own public key; only RS256 accepted{"sub":"ada","memberships":[…],"exp":…} as standard base64Path /twin/buildings becomes /buildingsData

Why the edge checks once: the services behind it never verify a signature; they read the header. The cluster does the same with Istio, so a service runs unchanged in both places: Kubernetes & Istio.

gateway lists five services in depends_on with required: false: it starts even when they are left out, and finds them when they appear, because Caddy looks up each name per request.

-----

.env: what just stack env writes

Every dev and start runs env first. Each script appends only what is missing, so a second run changes nothing except RUST_VERSION.

create.shvapid.shtoken.shconfig.shlangfuse.shkeycloak.shcontrolplane.shgateway-key.shingest-key.shtelemetry-db.shrust.shScriptAn empty .env, mode 600VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY, VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY, VITE_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY, a P-256 key pair; checks the lengths 87 and 43EVAL_JWT_SECRET, 32 random bytes, local evals onlyBACKEND_PORT=80, FRONTEND_PORT=8080, DEV_URL=http://localhost; asks for OPENROUTER_API_KEYLangfuse keys, salt, passwordsKEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD, KEYCLOAK_DB_PASSWORD, empty Google client fieldsINTERNAL_SIGNING_SECRET, TENANCY_DB_PASSWORD, REGISTRY_DB_PASSWORDsecrets/gateway-dev-key.pem, a 2048-bit RSA key, only if missingTELEMETRY_INGEST_SECRET, TELEMETRY_DEVICE_MASTER_KEYTELEMETRY_DB_PASSWORDRUST_VERSION, rewritten every run so a bump in .mise.toml reaches the buildWrites

The RSA key is kept on disk, not regenerated: a new key would make every signed-in cookie invalid.

-----

Live reload

RustGoagentfrontendLanguagesync ./srcsync ./sync ./appsync ./srcWatch rulecargo watch -x run rebuilds the service crate onlyair rebuilds and restartsuvicorn --reloadVite dev server, npm run devOn a source changeCargo.toml, Cargo.lock: rebuild the imagego.mod: rebuildpyproject.toml: rebuildpackage.json: rebuildOn a dependency change

- Rust has no target/ volume. The dev image already holds a fresh build; a volume over target/ would hide it, and every dependency change would compile twice.
- Go shares two volumes across the four services: go-mod-cache (/go/pkg/mod) and go-build-cache (/root/.cache/go-build). Go locks inside the cache folders, so four containers can use them at once.
- Mongo runs with --wiredTigerCacheSizeGB 0.25. Without it each of the four instances may grow towards half the host’s memory.

Published host ports

Only the dev overrides publish database ports. Two services on one host port stop the whole up.

8080805432, 5433, 5434, 543527017, 27019, 27020, 270216379, 9092, 80903001, 3002, 30033030Portgatewayclient (frontend)telemetry-db, tenancy-db, registry-db, agent-dbtwin-db, notification-db, dashboard-db, chat-dbredis, kafka, keycloaksensor-simulator, aq-simulator, ap-simulatorlangfuse-webService

-----

Test stacks

One service: just test <svc>-integration



chatdigital-twinnotificationsockettelemetrydashboardServicechat-integration-testsdigital-twin-integration-testsnotification-integration-testssocket-integration-teststelemetry-integration-testsdashboard-integration-testsProjectMongoDBMongoDBMongoDB, Redis, KafkaRedisTimescaleDB, Redis, KafkaMongoDB, RedisInfra

- Own project name: it never touches a running just stack dev.
- trap … EXIT: under set -e, a failed up would exit before a trailing down.
- The tests talk to containers by name, never through a host port.

Acceptance: just test integration

backend/acceptance/run-integration-tests.sh writes compose.integration-tests.runtime.yml:

docker/rust-base/docker-compose.ymlbackend/acceptance/docker-compose.infra.ymlbackend/{telemetry,socket,dashboard}/docker-compose.ymlbackend/acceptance/docker-compose.integration.ymlIncluded fileThe Rust build imageredis, kafkaThe three real servicesStubs for digital-twin and claims-gateway (nginx), the real Caddy gateway, and the integration-tests runnerGives

- The real Caddyfile is mounted, so backend/acceptance/edge/ tests the edge that ships.
- Stub claims-gateway answers /verify with a fixed 401 and a marker, so a test can tell an edge refusal from a service one.
- It generates the telemetry keys itself, so it runs without just stack env.

-----

Traps

- just stack dev does not rebuild by default. Only --build, or a watched rebuild file, rebuilds an image. A Dockerfile change needs --build.
- --no-simulators leaves telemetry’s SIMULATORS list as is. Starting a simulation then fails to reach them.
- A root service cannot leave by folder. prometheus, grafana, keycloak go only by name, which is why --no-metrics exists.
- container_name is global. crowd-vision-socket is shared by the dev stack and the acceptance stack; the acceptance script removes a stopped one, never a running one.
- Renaming a volume empties the service. Compose names the real volume after project and key: see Naming.

Related: Docker Images, Kubernetes & Istio, Build System.

entries.title: Kubernetes & Istio
entries.content:
Kubernetes & Istio

Clusterk3dNamespacePodDeploymentStatefulSetInit containerSecret, ConfigMapIstioAmbient modeztunnelWaypointGateway APImTLSWordMachines Kubernetes runs containers onRuns a small Kubernetes (k3s) inside Docker containersA named box that groups a cluster’s objectsOne or more containers that start and stop togetherKeeps N copies of a stateless pod runningLike a Deployment, but each pod keeps its own diskRuns to the end before the main container startsValues handed to pods as environment variables; a Secret for private onesA service mesh: it carries, encrypts and checks traffic between podsIstio without a proxy in each pod: one ztunnel per node does the workIstio’s per-node proxy: mutual TLS and identity checks between podsAn optional per-namespace proxy for HTTP rules inside the meshKubernetes’ standard way to describe an entry point and its routesBoth sides of a connection prove who they are with certificatesMeaningcrowdvision, made by k3dOne server nodecrowdvisiontelemetry-7f9c…k8s/deployments/telemetry.ymlk8s/stateful/telemetry-db.ymlwait-for-dbtelemetry-secret, common-configAmbient modeistio.io/dataplane-mode: ambientA DaemonSetNot used hereGateway, HTTPRoutePeerAuthentication STRICTExample

The cluster setup mirrors Docker Compose: same images, same routes, same claims header. Only the edge changes, from Caddy to Istio.

-----

What is in k8s/

namespace.ymlconfigmaps/common.ymlstateful/deployments/monitoring/istio-peer-authentication.ymlistio-gateway.ymlistio-request-authentication.ymlistio-agent-authz.ymlPathNamespace crowdvision, labelled istio.io/dataplane-mode: ambientcommon-config: PORT, REDIS_URL, KAFKA_BROKERS, service URLs, PUBLIC_URL=http://crowdvision.local10 StatefulSets: twin-db, notification-db, dashboard-db, chat-db (MongoDB), telemetry-db (TimescaleDB), agent-db (pgvector), registry-db, tenancy-db (Postgres), redis, kafka12 Deployments and their Services: the 11 backend services and frontendprometheus (with its ServiceAccount, ClusterRole and scrape config), grafanaSTRICT mTLS for the whole namespaceThe Gateway and one HTTPRoute per pathJWT check at the edge, and the policy saying which paths need itOnly the edge and chat may call agentHolds

Not in the cluster: Keycloak, the Langfuse stack, the simulators, ap-collector, the docs ingester.

A Deployment, piece by piece

k8s/deployments/telemetry.yml:

replicasinitContainersimagesecurityContextenvFromprobesresourcesannotationsPart1wait-for-db: until nc -z telemetry-db 5432ghcr.io/nickghignatti/crowdvision-telemetry:latest, IfNotPresentallowPrivilegeEscalation: false, readOnlyRootFilesystem: truetelemetry-secret, common-confighttpGet /health on 3000: ready after 10 s, alive every 20 sasks 100m CPU, 128 Mi; capped at 500m, 256 Miprometheus.io/scrape: "true"ValueEvery service runs one copyThe service crashes if its database is not up yetUses an image imported by just k8s load without asking GHCRNothing in the container can be changed; /tmp is an emptyDirPrivate values, then shared onesNo command inside the image: distroless has no shellPrometheus finds the podWhy

Services that need more than one dependency get one init container per dependency: dashboard waits for dashboard-db, redis, telemetry and digital-twin, in that order.

-----

just k8s setup: the first time



24578–9Step-p "80:80@loadbalancer" -p "443:443@loadbalancer" --api-port 6550 --k3s-arg "--disable=traefik@server:0". Traefik is off because Istio is the entry pointThe CRDs teach the cluster what a Gateway and an HTTPRoute are--set values.cni.cniConfDir=/var/lib/rancher/k3s/agent/etc/cni/net.d --set values.cni.cniBinDir=/bin. istioctl is pinned to 1.31.3 in .mise.tomlThe namespace label enrolls every pod in ambient mode at creation: no restart neededSee the secrets table belowDetail

just k8s apply: the order

123456789#namespace.ymlconfigmaps/stateful/deployments/istio-peer-authentication.ymlistio-gateway.ymlistio-request-authentication.ymlistio-agent-authz.ymlmonitoring/FileEverything lives in itDeployments read it at startDatabases first: the init containers wait for themCreates chat’s ServiceAccount, which step 8 namesmTLS onCreates the edge workload the next two selectWhy here

Every step is kubectl apply: running it again changes only what differs.

Secrets

scripts/k8s/k8s-secrets.sh reads .env, checks every required key before writing anything, then writes each secret with kubectl create secret … --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -, so it can run again.

telemetry-secretnotification-secretregistry-secret, tenancy-secretprovisioner-secretclaims-gateway-secretclaims-gateway-keyagent-secretchat-secret, digital-twin-secret, dashboard-secret*-db-secretgrafana-secretghcr-pull-secretSecretDATABASE_URL, TELEMETRY_DEVICE_MASTER_KEY, and TELEMETRY_INGEST_SECRET only if setMONGO_URI, VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY, VAPID_PRIVATE_KEYDATABASE_URL, INTERNAL_SIGNING_SECRETINTERNAL_SIGNING_SECRETINTERNAL_SIGNING_SECRET, REGISTRATION_CLIENT_SECRETsecrets/gateway-dev-key.pem, from diskGOOGLE_API_KEY, DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, POSTGRES_URLMONGO_URIThe database’s own user and passwordAdmin user and password, default admin / crowdvisionOnly when GHCR_USERNAME and GHCR_TOKEN are set; GHCR images are publicHolds

-----

A request through Istio



123–4567–8StepThe token is read from Authorization: Bearer … or the authentication_token cookiejwksUri points at the gateway’s own /gateway/* route, so the key fetch also goes through the meshoutputPayloadToHeader: x-gateway-claims; forwardOriginalToken: false, so the JWT itself goes no furtherGated paths need a request principal from issuer cv-gatewayReplacePrefixMatch: /, same as Caddy’s handle_pathztunnel on each node wraps pod-to-pod traffic in mTLS; plain text is refusedWhat happens

Which paths need a token



agent

Remove x-gateway-claimsagent-callersRuleagent-route, RequestHeaderModifieristio-agent-authz.ymlWhereThe edge never passes claims to agentOnly ServiceAccounts crowdvision-gateway-istio and chat may open a connectionEffect

Why: agent trusts the claims header without a signature. Only chat may hand it one; ztunnel checks the caller’s identity, which a pod cannot fake.

-----

Parity with Compose

EdgeExtra hop per requestHeader services readPrefix removalUngated telemetry paths/agent claimsSSE on /chatBetween servicesCaddy forward_auth to claims-gateway /verifyYesx-gateway-claimshandle_path3 exact handle blocks in Caddyfileheader_up -X-Gateway-Claimsflush_interval -1Plain HTTP on the Compose networkComposeIstio RequestAuthentication at the gatewayNo: the gateway has the keysx-gateway-claimsURLRewrite ReplacePrefixMatch3 exact paths in require-gateway-jwtRequestHeaderModifier removetimeouts.request: 120smTLS through ztunnelCluster

The three exact telemetry paths are written twice, by hand. backend/acceptance/edge/ tests the Caddy side; nothing tests the Istio side.

-----

Checks

just k8s validateci-k8sci-k8sci-k8sWherekubectl apply --dry-run=clientkubeconform 0.6.7, -strict, Kubernetes 1.32.0pluto 5.24.0kube-score 1.20.0ToolEach file parses and is accepted, without touching the clusterEvery manifest against its schema; Istio and Gateway API kinds through the datree CRD catalogNo API version that Kubernetes removedGood practice. Switched off: network policy, disruption budget, user and group id, read-only root, image tag, pull policy, identical probesChecks

-----

Day to day

just k8s buildjust k8s loadjust k8s push, build-pushjust k8s statusjust k8s logs <svc>just k8s restart <svc>, restart-alljust k8s rollout <svc>just k8s stop, startjust k8s hostsjust k8s deleteRecipeBuilds 12 images tagged ghcr.io/nickghignatti/crowdvision-*:latestImports them into k3d, no registryPushes them to GHCRkubectl get all -n crowdvisionFollows logs by label app=<svc>Rolling restart: picks up a new :latestWaits for a rollout to finishPauses and resumes the cluster; data keptPrints 127.0.0.1   crowdvision.local for the hosts fileDeletes the namespace and every volume in it. No undoDoes

-----

Traps

- Wrong CNI path, broken node. k3d’s containerd looks for CNI plugins in /bin. Another path makes every pod fail with failed to find plugin "istio-cni", and each failed retry leaks an address until no IP addresses available in range set. Only a new cluster fixes that.
- Git Bash rewrites /bin. Run straight from Git Bash, istioctl --set values.cni.cniBinDir=/bin gets a Windows path. just runs recipes through PowerShell on Windows, which does not.
- No Keycloak in the cluster. claims-gateway looks for it at host.k3d.internal:8090, so Keycloak must run from Compose, or sign-in fails at start.
- A missing token gives a different status. Caddy answers 401 from /verify; Istio’s policy denies a gated path with no principal by its own refusal, not by claims-gateway.
- An expired cookie may block everything. Istio rejects a request whose token is present but invalid, on any path. The cookie has no Max-Age, so an expired JWT stays in the browser. Not tested here.
- The cookie is Secure. Browsers keep it over plain http only for localhost, and the cluster is reached at http://crowdvision.local. Not tested here.
- Image tags drift. grafana is 13.2.4 in Compose and 13.2.1 in the cluster; redis 8.10.2 and 8.10.1.
- dashboard-secret names contractsdb. dashboard ignores the database in its URI and opens crowdvision anyway.

Related: Docker Images, Docker Compose, CI.

entries.title: GitHub Actions CI
entries.content:
GitHub Actions CI

WorkflowJobLegReusable workflowComposite actionRunnerPath filterMatrixArtifactGHCRRulesetWordOne YAML file in .github/workflows/, started by an eventOne unit of work in a workflow, on its own runnerA job of the gate that checks one part of the repoA workflow other workflows call with uses:, like a functionA short list of steps shared by several workflowsThe fresh virtual machine a job runs onA rule that says “this area changed” when a file under a path changedOne job run once per item of a listA file a job uploads so a later job can download itGitHub’s container registry, where images are storedGitHub settings that say what a merge into master needsMeaningci-gate.ymlchanges, telemetryThe twin legtpl-rust-ci.yml.github/actions/setup-rustubuntu-latest; Rust jobs and the acceptance suite pin ubuntu-22.04: MongoDB 8 refuses to start on Linux kernels 6.19 to 7.0.13 (SERVER-121912), and the 24.04 and 26.04 runners ship 7.0.0backend/telemetry/**One Docker build per changed imagebinary-telemetryghcr.io/nickghignatti/crowdvision-telemetry“CI Passed” must be greenExample

CrowdVision’s CI runs on GitHub Actions. It checks every pull request into master, then publishes images, coverage and the docs site after the merge. Every workflow reads one file to know the services: .github/services.json.

Related pages: Release Please, Dependencies & Security.

-----

The workflows

Each file name starts with its kind.

ci-tpl-cd-maint-KindA pull request, or a call from ci-gate.ymlA call only: reusable workflow per languageA push to masterA weekly timerStarted byci-gate, ci-frontend, ci-docker, ci-k8s, ci-infra, ci-simulators, ci-acceptance, ci-docs, ci-dependency-review, ci-codeqltpl-rust-ci, tpl-go-ci, tpl-python-ci, tpl-node-ci, tpl-*-coveragecd-registry, cd-release, cd-coverage, cd-documentationmaint-renovate, maint-cleanupFiles

ci-gate.ymlci-codeql.ymlcd-registry.ymlcd-release.ymlcd-coverage.ymlcd-documentation.ymlmaint-renovate.ymlmaint-cleanup.ymlWorkflowPR into masterPR into master, Monday 03:00, by handPush to master touching backend/, simulators/, frontend/Every push to masterEvery push to master, by handPush to master touching the docsMonday 02:00, by handSunday 02:00, by handWhenFinds what changed, runs only those checks, reports one result: CI PassedSecurity scan of the source, 4 languagesPublishes images to GHCRRelease Please: release PR, tag, changelogMeasures coverage, publishes it on branch coverage-dataBuilds this site, publishes it to GitHub PagesOpens dependency update PRsDeletes old image versions from GHCR, keeps 3 and latestWhat it does

-----

The service list: .github/services.json

One entry per buildable part. Every workflow reads it, so a new service is one entry, not an edit in each workflow.

keydirlangimagecd_context, dockerfileneeds_mongo, needs_redis, needs_postgres, needs_kafkabuilds_binarydepends_onciFieldShort name, also the path filter nameWhere it livesPicks the reusable workflow and the Docker recipeImage name; no field means no imageBuild context and Dockerfile for cd-registryContainers the Rust tests needfalse for librariesFolders it builds or tests from; their changes select it too. Must cover every local replace and Cargo pathfalse: no gate leg and no PR imageMeaningtwinbackend/digital-twinrust, go, python, node, frontendcrowdvision-twin., backend/digital-twin/Dockerfilenotification: Mongo, Redis, Kafkaauth-contractstenancy: backend/libs/auth-middleware, schemas/fixturesthe three simulatorsExample

Example. telemetry has needs_redis, needs_postgres, needs_kafka. Its gate leg starts Redis, TimescaleDB and Kafka before the integration tests. socket has only needs_redis, so its leg starts Redis only.

-----

A pull request, from push to green



234578101415Stepconcurrency: ci-gate-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true: a new push stops the old run.github/actions/filter-services runs scripts/service-filters.py: one filter per entry, its dir plus its depends_on, for example telemetry: + - "backend/telemetry/**", - "schemas/claims-schema/**", - "schemas/fixtures/**", … The script fails the job first if depends_on disagrees with the code. Then the action adds the gate’s own filters: k8s, ci, infra, simulators, acceptance, docs, depsOutput changes, a JSON list, for example ["telemetry","deps"]Changed keys with an image and no ci: false, for example {"include":[{"context":"./backend/telemetry","image":"crowdvision-telemetry","lang":"rust"}]}One job per changed service. Libraries and schema crates also have legs, with builds_binary: falseEach extra area has its own leg, see belowci-docker.yml, one matrix entry per image, see “Images on a pull request”A shell loop over needs.*.resultThe only required check in the master ruleset is CI PassedWhat happens, with real values

Which legs run

A leg runs when its own dir changed, or a folder in its depends_on changed. Every service leg’s condition is just its own key; the dependencies live in .github/services.json, not in ci-gate.yml.



depends_on cannot drift from the code. Before printing the filters, scripts/service-filters.py fails the changes job when:

- a depends_on folder does not exist, for example after a rename;
- a go.mod replace ... => ../path or a Cargo.toml path = "../path" points outside the service at a folder no depends_on covers.

A listed service passes its own service dirs on: tenancy lists auth-middleware, so it is also selected by auth-contracts. Plain folders do not pass on: auth-contracts’ fixtures feed its own tests, not the code its consumers compile.

Why: a dependency bump in auth-middleware once passed its own leg, skipped tenancy and claims-gateway, and left both unbuildable on master (missing go.sum entry), unnoticed until a later run rebuilt every service. The hand-written conditions it slipped through had four more holes of the same kind.

What the current depends_on gives:

backend/libs/auth-contractsbackend/libs/auth-middlewarebackend/libs/auth-policyschemas/claims-schemaschemas/telemetry-schemaschemas/twin-schemaschemas/fixtures/**, schemas/json/**Change inauth-middleware, auth-policy, claims-gateway, provisioner, registry, tenancyclaims-gateway, tenancytenancychat, notification, telemetry, socket, twin, dashboardnotification, telemetry, socket, twin, dashboardtelemetry, socket, twinEvery leg whose tests replay a fixture: frontend, agent, ap-collector, tenancy, auth-contracts, the four schema crates, chat, notification, telemetry, socket, twin, and the simulators legLegs that also runThey build against its source through a local replaceLocal replace; its dependency versions must reach their go.sumLocal replace: the Cedar bundle tenancy evaluatesEvery Rust service parses claims with itThey share the tick and alert shapesRegistration, Wi-Fi and device shapesA fixture change must fail every language that disagreesWhy

Example. A PR changes only schemas/twin-schema/src/wifi.rs. Keys changed: twin-schema, telemetry, socket, twin. Legs that run: those four. PR images built: crowdvision-telemetry, crowdvision-socket, crowdvision-twin, because they compile the crate; twin-schema has no image.

Why one gate job

ci-passed waits for every leg with if: always(), so it runs even when legs are skipped.

changes must be successEvery other result must be success or skippedOnly CI Passed is requiredRuleIf it failed, every leg was skipped without being judged. Green there would be a lieA list of good results, not of bad ones: cancelled or any new value fails tooThe ruleset names one check, so adding or removing a leg never touches GitHub settingsWhy

A leg nobody waits for passes silently
-----
needs: cannot be computed, so every service job is written three times in ci-gate.yml: as a job, in docker.needs, in ci-passed.needs. A job missing from a list still runs, but the gate goes green without it. scripts/check-workflow-registry.py, run by the workflows-lint leg and by just lint workflows (also before just lint all and just lint affected), compares the three lists with services.json and fails on any gap.

-----

The language legs

Each language has one reusable workflow. The gate calls it with service_key and working_directory.

tpl-rust-ci.yml



3478911Stepsetup-mongo runs mongo:8.3.9, setup-redis runs redis:8.10.1-alpine, each waits until it answersVersion from the rust = "…" line of .mise.toml. Swatinem/rust-cache, key rust-ci-telemetryIgnores RUSTSEC-2023-0071 and RUSTSEC-2026-0387: both reach notification through web-push and have no usable fix--lib fails on a crate with no lib.rs, so dashboard runs --binsRuns each tests/*.rs by name, so unit tests are not run twice. Env: MONGO_URI=mongodb://localhost:27017, REDIS_URL, DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:telemetry@localhost:5432/telemetrydb, KAFKA_BROKERS=localhost:9092The binary is named after the folder: backend/digital-twin gives digital-twinDetail

The other languages

tpl-go-ci.ymltpl-python-ci.ymlci-frontend.ymltpl-node-ci.ymlWorkflowsetup-go (version from .mise.toml, Go module cache), gofmt -l loop, go vet, govulncheck, go build, go test -tags=integration ./..., build ./cmd/...setup-python (.python-version, uv cache, uv sync --locked), ruff check, ruff format --check, pyright, uv audit, pytestJob quality: npm ci, lint, type-check, npm audit --omit=dev. Job test: Vitest in 3 shardsLint, build, test, audit, upload dist-<key>Steps, in orderEverything except govulncheck, which is continue-on-errorEverything. Builds no artifactEverything except the full npm audit including dev depsNot called by any workflowBlocks on

- gofmt -l lists bad files and still exits 0, so the step loops over its output and fails itself.
- -tags=integration adds the testcontainers suites to the normal run. Without the tag those files compile nowhere.

Other legs of the gate

k8s (ci-k8s.yml)infra (ci-infra.yml)simulators (ci-simulators.yml)acceptance (ci-acceptance.yml)docs (ci-docs.yml)dependency-reviewworkflows-lintLegk8s/**scripts/**, tooling/**, Justfilesimulators/**backend/acceptance/**, Caddyfile, k8s/istio-request-authentication.yml, telemetry, socket, dashboard, devices/ap-collectordocumentation/**, api/**, the docs recipe, .mise.tomlAny manifest or lockfile.github/**Runs whenkubeconform -strict against Kubernetes 1.32.0 plus the CRD catalog for Istio kinds, pluto for removed APIs, kube-score with 7 tests ignorednode --check on JS, bash -n on shell, each scripts/test_*.py, just --summarysensor-simulator: lint, build, test. aq-simulator and ap-simulator: ruff check, pyright, uv audit, pytestbackend/acceptance/run-integration-tests.sh: a composed stack with a real Caddy edge. 45 min limit, the slowest legjust docs build, with the Quarkdown version read from .mise.tomlSee Dependencies & Securityactionlint (shellcheck off), zizmor --min-severity medium, check-workflow-registry.pyWhat it checks

-----

Images on a pull request

ci-docker.yml runs after the legs, once per changed image, when no leg failed.



go, rustpythonfrontendlang.github/docker/Dockerfile.ci: alpine, apk upgrade, copy the binaryThe service’s own Dockerfile, no cachefrontend/DockerfileDockerfile..frontendContextThe leg’s binary artifactSourceSourceInput

- if: !cancelled() && !contains(needs.*.result, 'failure'): a skipped leg in needs would otherwise skip this job too, and some leg is skipped on nearly every PR.
- Python images build with no-cache, so the apt upgrade in their Dockerfile runs every time instead of reusing an old layer.

-----

A merge, through to published images



358101114Stepworkflow_dispatch with service: all or a list such as twin,frontend. A change to services.json or cd-registry.yml selects every imageTag = rust pin from .mise.toml + first 12 characters of the sha256 of docker/rust-base/Dockerfile. An unchanged base is never rebuiltA squash merge makes a new commit, so the PR’s head SHA is looked up through the APISame Trivy settings as on the PR; the result also goes to the Security tabA registry-side copy of the manifest: the published image is exactly the one scanned on the PRHappens on a manual run, or when the PR image is missing. frontend gets VITE_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY as a build argDetail

The image shipped is the CI image, not the service Dockerfile
-----
For Go and Rust, the promoted image is the one built on the pull request from .github/docker/Dockerfile.ci: Alpine plus the binary from the leg. The service’s own Dockerfile (with rust-base or a Go builder) is used only when no PR image exists. A change that only edits a service Dockerfile therefore does not change what runs after a normal merge.

-----

Coverage after a merge

cd-coverage.yml measures coverage on master only. Pull requests never measure it, and no threshold blocks anything.

1. load-registry path-filters the push and splits the changed services by lang into four lists.
2. One tpl-<lang>-coverage.yml call per non-empty list. An empty list skips the job: GitHub fails a reusable workflow called with an empty matrix.
3. publish downloads the reports and fetches the previous coverage-counts.json and reports/ from branch coverage-data.
4. scripts/coverage-summary.py merges new counts over the old ones and rewrites reports/<service>.json for the services that ran, so unchanged services keep their numbers and their per-file report.
5. The result, badge.json, summary.json, coverage-counts.json and reports/, is force-pushed as a single commit to coverage-data, with 3 attempts.

Example. A push changes telemetry only. rust gets one entry, node, python, go are skipped. The badge is recomputed from the new telemetry counts plus last run’s counts for every other service.

-----

Speed: caches and skipping

Skip unchanged partsRustGoPythonNodeDockerNo double buildStop stale runsWhatPath filters per service; ci-passed treats skipped as fineSwatinem/rust-cache, one key per serviceactions/setup-go cache keyed on go.sumsetup-uv cache keyed on uv.lockactions/setup-node npm cache keyed on package-lock.jsontype=gha layer cache, scoped per image on PRsGo and Rust images reuse the leg’s binary; cd-registry promotes the PR imagecancel-in-progress on the gate and on CodeQLHow

-----

Permissions

Read-only token by defaultpackages: write only where pushingCodeQL in its own workflowpersist-credentials: false on every checkoutValues through env:, never inline in run:Third-party actions pinned to a commit SHAPAT secretsRuleci-gate.yml: contents: read, pull-requests: readdocker job, cd-registry, maint-cleanupci-codeql.yml with security-events: writeAll workflowsAll workflowsAll workflowsSEMANTIC_RELEASE_TOKEN, RENOVATE_TOKENWhereA PR’s code runs with the smallest rightsOnly those touch GHCRA called workflow cannot get more rights than its caller, and the gate stays read-onlyThe token is not left on disk for later stepsStops template injection; zizmor checks itA tag can be moved to other code; a SHA cannotPRs opened with the default token start no workflowsWhy

-----

What blocks a merge into master

From the repository rulesets:

Required checkCode scanningMerge methodReviewsBranchRuleCI Passed, up to date with masterCodeQL: security alerts high or higher, or any error-level alertSquash only, linear historyA pull request is required; 0 approvalsNo deletion, no force pushValue

-----

Traps

- tpl-node-ci.yml and .github/actions/filter-languages are unused. No workflow calls them.
- govulncheck never blocks. Its step has continue-on-error: true.
- .trivyignore is empty. Any fixable HIGH or CRITICAL OS finding fails the image job; a waiver needs a line there with its reason.
- A Trivy finding can appear with no code change. The scan reads today’s advisory database, so an old base image can fail tomorrow.
- The gate does not run on a push to master. Only on pull requests. cd-* workflows assume the PR already passed.

-----

Reproducing locally

A service legAll changed partsworkflows-lint registry checkdocsacceptanceLockfiles and auditCI legjust test <svc>, then just test <svc>-integrationjust test affected, just lint affectedjust lint workflowsjust docs buildjust test integrationjust setup deps-check, just setup auditLocal command

The gate skill runs the checks in CI order and stops at the first failure.

entries.title: Release Please
entries.content:
Release Please

Conventional CommitTypeScopeBreaking changeComponentManifestRelease PRPre-majorPrereleaseWordA commit title that starts with its kindThe kind of change, before the colonThe part changed, in bracketsA change that needs users to adapt; ! after the type, or a BREAKING CHANGE: lineOne package with its own versionThe file that holds the last released version of each componentThe pull request Release Please keeps open with the next versions and changelogA version below 1.0.0A version with a suffix that marks it unfinishedMeaningfeat(twin): add floor pickerfeat, fix, choretwin, gatewayfeat(gateway)!: drop /v1backend/chat, component chat.release-please-manifest.jsonchore: release master0.3.1-alpha-alphaExample

Release Please turns commit titles into version numbers and changelogs. Nobody picks a version by hand: the commits merged since the last release decide it. The tool runs in cd-release.yml on every push to master.

Related pages: GitHub Actions CI, commit scopes in Naming.

-----

Files

.github/workflows/cd-release.ymlrelease-please-config.json.release-please-manifest.jsonCHANGELOG.mdbackend/digital-twin/CHANGELOG.mdFileRuns googleapis/release-please-action with the two files below, token SEMANTIC_RELEASE_TOKENOne entry per component: path, release-type, component, optionsLast released version per path, written by the release PRRoot changelog, one section per releaseThe only component changelog so farHolds

Components

.frontendbackend/chat, notification, telemetry, socket, digital-twin, dashboardbackend/agentbackend/claims-gateway, provisioner, registry, tenancy, backend/libs/*Pathsimplenoderustpythongorelease-typenone, only CHANGELOG.md and the manifestpackage.json, package-lock.jsonCargo.toml, Cargo.lockpyproject.tomlnone: Go modules carry no version; only the changelogVersion file it bumpsYes: v0.3.1-alphaNoNoNoNoOwn tag and GitHub release

- Every component except . has skip-github-release: true. Only the root makes a Git tag and a GitHub release.
- schemas/*, the simulators and backend/acceptance are not components: their commits only count for the root.

Root options

prerelease: true, prerelease-type: alphabump-minor-pre-major: truebump-patch-for-minor-pre-major: trueOptionVersions carry -alphaBelow 1.0.0, a breaking change bumps the minor, not the majorBelow 1.0.0, a feat bumps the patch, not the minorEffect

-----

From commit type to version

fix:feat:feat!: or BREAKING CHANGE:docs, chore, ci, refactor, test, style, perf, buildNo type, or a typo like feet:Commitpatch: 1.4.2 → 1.4.3minor: 1.4.2 → 1.5.0major: 1.4.2 → 2.0.0nothingnothing, no errorAbove 1.0.0patchpatch: 0.3.0-alpha → 0.3.1-alphaminor: 0.1.0-alpha → 0.2.0-alphanothingnothing, no errorRoot today, below 1.0.0

The highest bump among the commits wins.

Example, from CHANGELOG.md.

- 0.2.0-alpha → 0.3.0-alpha: one feat, plus earlier breaking changes. Breaking below 1.0.0 gives a minor bump.
- 0.3.0-alpha → 0.3.1-alpha: one feat(…) only, “building upload notification”. feat below 1.0.0 gives a patch bump.

Which component a commit counts for

A commit counts for every component whose path holds a file it changed, and always for ..

Example. feat(twin): support multi-floor buildings changes backend/digital-twin/src/… and frontend/src/….

- backend/digital-twin: feat, so its version goes up.
- frontend: same commit, so its version goes up too.
- .: also goes up, and gets the changelog line.

The scope in the title is only text for the changelog. Release Please picks components by file paths, never by scope.

-----

The release flow



467811StepThe last release of each path is found through the merged release PR and the manifestOne PR for all components, the Merge plugin. Title chore: release master. Its diff: CHANGELOG.md files, version files, .release-please-manifest.jsonOpened with SEMANTIC_RELEASE_TOKEN, a personal token: a PR made with the default GITHUB_TOKEN starts no workflows, and could never pass the gateA normal squash merge, so cd-registry also runs on itOnly for .; components have skip-github-releaseDetail

What each run decides



-----

Traps

Releases are stuck
-----
Every cd-release run since release PR #337 ends with “There are untagged, merged release PRs outstanding – aborting”, and the job still shows green. #337 released only one component, at the old path backend/twin-service, and still carries the label autorelease: pending. That path is no longer in the config, so Release Please can never tag it, and waits for it on every run. No release PR has opened since. Changing the label of #337 to autorelease: tagged by hand unblocks it.

- A wrong title fails silently. Nothing in CI checks commit titles. A typo gives no release and no error.
- Only the squash title counts. master allows squash merges only, so the PR title becomes the commit Release Please reads. Commit titles inside the branch do not matter.
- Go versions live only in the changelog. A Go module has no version field, so the manifest is the only record.
- A renamed folder is a new component. The release history is keyed by path. Renaming a folder needs the config, the manifest and the changelog path moved in the same change.
- Versions are not read at runtime. No service reports its version; the numbers exist for the changelog and for npm ci, which refuses a package.json and package-lock.json that disagree.

entries.title: Dependencies & Security
entries.content:
Dependencies & Security

ManifestLockfileIn syncAdvisoryAuditRenovateSASTTrivyWordThe file where a package lists what it needs, with allowed rangesThe exact version of every dependency, direct and indirect, written by the package managerThe lockfile matches the manifest, so an install changes nothingA published warning that a version has a security holeA scan of a lockfile against known advisoriesA bot that opens pull requests to update dependenciesScanning source code for security mistakes, without running itA scanner for the operating-system packages inside an imageMeaningCargo.toml, package.jsonCargo.lock, uv.locknpm ci passesRUSTSEC-2023-0071cargo auditchore(deps): update ciCodeQLapk packages in AlpineExample

Every package installs its own dependencies: there is no shared root lockfile. This page covers how versions are pinned, how they are updated, and which scans stop a known hole from reaching master.

Related pages: GitHub Actions CI, Release Please.

-----

Lockfiles per language

RustGoPythonNodeLanguagecargogouvnpmManagerCargo.lockgo.sumuv.lockpackage-lock.jsonLockfile6 services, 4 schemas/*-schema cratesclaims-gateway, registry, tenancy, auth-middleware, auth-policyagent, acceptance, ap-collector, aq-simulator, ap-simulatorfrontend, sensor-simulator, tooling/eslint-configWheremise exec -- cargo update in the crate, or let cargo add / cargo build write itmise exec -- go mod tidy in the modulemise exec -- uv lock in the projectnpm install --prefix <dir> --package-lock-only --cpu=x64 --os=linuxRegenerate with

- auth-contracts and provisioner have no go.sum: they need nothing outside the standard library and this repo.
- Never edit a lockfile by hand. Change the manifest, then let the manager write the lock.

Why Node locks are made for Linux

A lockfile written on a Mac or on Windows lists only that machine’s native packages. CI runs npm ci on Linux, finds a missing package, and fails. --cpu=x64 --os=linux writes the Linux entries whatever machine runs it.

Example. A developer on an Apple laptop adds a package to frontend:

1. npm install some-lib inside frontend/.
2. npm install --prefix frontend --package-lock-only --cpu=x64 --os=linux.
3. Commit package.json and package-lock.json together.

just setup clean-install does step 2 for every Node project at once, after deleting node_modules and the lock. It also runs uv lock for every Python project.

-----

Local checks

Two recipes run a moon task in every project.

just setup deps-checkjust setup auditRecipe:deps, :deps-check:auditmoon tasksRust cargo fetch + cargo check. Go go mod download. Python uv sync --locked. Node npm ciRust cargo audit. Python uv audit. TypeScript npm audit --audit-level=high --omit=devPer language



458Stepnpm ci: lockfile and package.json disagree. uv sync --locked: uv.lock is stale. go mod download: go.sum lacks a hashcargo check: the code no longer builds with the locked versionsAn advisory: Rust any, Python any, Node high or worse in production dependenciesWhat fails it

-----

In CI

Inside each language leg

Rust (tpl-rust-ci)Go (tpl-go-ci)Python (tpl-python-ci, simulators)Frontend (ci-frontend)Frontend, dev dependencies tooLegbuilds with Cargo.lockgo mod downloaduv sync --lockednpm ciLockfile checkcargo audit --ignore RUSTSEC-2023-0071 --ignore RUSTSEC-2026-0387govulncheck ./..., only for code paths actually calleduv auditnpm audit --audit-level=high --omit=devnpm audit --audit-level=highAuditYes, vulnerabilities only; “unmaintained” and “yanked” are warningsNo, continue-on-errorYesYesNo, only loggedBlocks the PR?

dependency-review: what this PR adds

Runs when a PR changes any manifest or lockfile (filter deps in ci-gate.yml).

- actions/dependency-review-action, fail-on-severity: high.
- It compares the PR with master and fails only on new dependencies with a high or critical advisory.
- The audits above look at the whole lockfile; this check names the exact package the PR brought in.

CodeQL: the source code

ci-codeql.yml, outside the gate.

WhenLanguagesQueriesBlocks a mergeSettingEvery PR into master, Monday 03:00, by handjavascript-typescript, python, rust with build-mode: none; go with autobuildsecurity-extendedYes, through the ruleset: security alerts high or higherValue

Trivy: the image

Runs on every image a PR changes, and again before cd-registry publishes.

- vuln-type: os: only operating-system packages. Language packages are already covered by the audits above.
- severity: HIGH,CRITICAL, ignore-unfixed: true: only holes that have a fix fail the job.
- .trivyignore holds waived advisories, one per line with its reason. It is empty.
- Images upgrade their OS packages while building: apk --no-cache upgrade in .github/docker/Dockerfile.ci, apt-get upgrade in the Python Dockerfiles. A base image is often older than its own package mirror.

-----

Renovate: updates arrive as pull requests

maint-renovate.yml runs Renovate every Monday at 02:00 (Europe/Rome rules in renovate.json), or by hand.



234510StepRENOVATE_TOKEN is a personal token: a PR made with the default token would start no workflowManagers found: cargo, gomod, npm, pep621 with uv.lock, Dockerfile FROM tags, github-actions SHAs, mise tools in .mise.toml, pip_requirements in .github/requirements-lint.txtSee the grouping rules belowRenovate runs the package manager itself, so the lockfile is regenerated, never hand-editedRenovate’s titles are Conventional Commits. fix(deps) bumps a patch; chore(deps) bumps nothingDetail

Grouping rules

Major updateMinor, patch, pin, digest under one folderGitHub Actions and mise toolsPython itselfNew Python minorLimitsRuleIts own PR, labels dependencies, majorOne PR per folder: frontend, each backend/* service, each backend/libs/*, backend/acceptance (backend-tests), simulators, toolingOne PR, group ciOne PR for every pin (.python-version, .mise.toml, images), so CI never tests a Python the images do not shipOpened only after approval on the dependency dashboard issue: compiled packages publish wheels laterprConcurrentLimit: 0, prHourlyLimit: 0: no capEffect

Example. Renovate finds redis 8.10.1 → 8.10.3 in a compose file and a new actions/checkout SHA.

- redis lives in a Docker tag outside any grouped folder: its own PR, “chore(deps): update redis docker tag to v8.10.3”.
- actions/checkout matches the github-actions manager: it joins the ci group, “chore(deps): update ci”.

-----

Updating by hand

1. Change the version in the manifest.
2. Regenerate the lockfile with the command in the table at the top.
3. Run just setup deps-check and just setup audit.
4. Run the package’s tests: just test <svc>.
5. Open the PR. The gate runs the package’s leg and dependency-review.

For Rust and Go toolchains, the version is pinned in .mise.toml, and CI reads the same pin. A Go bump also moves the golang tag in the four Go Dockerfiles.

-----

Traps

- just setup audit skips Go. No Go project defines an audit task in .moon/tasks/go.yml. Only CI runs govulncheck, and its result never blocks.
- Local cargo audit has no ignore list. CI ignores RUSTSEC-2023-0071 and RUSTSEC-2026-0387; the moon task does not. just setup audit can fail on notification while its CI leg passes.
- cargo check does not prove Cargo.lock is in sync. Without --locked, cargo updates a stale lock quietly instead of failing, in CI as well as locally.
- No relock for Rust or Go. just setup clean-install rewrites only Node and Python lockfiles.
- An audit can fail with no change. Advisories are published every day; an old lockfile can fail tomorrow. Fix by updating, or by ignoring with a reason in the workflow.

entries.title: Setting Up the Environment
entries.content:
Setting Up the Environment

.envSecretKeycloakVAPID keysLangfusek3dWordOne file at the repo root holding every local setting and secretA random value two parts share, so each can trust the otherThe sign-in serverThe key pair a browser uses to accept Web Push from notificationA web page that shows every step the assistant tookA small Kubernetes cluster that runs inside DockerMeaningBACKEND_PORT=80INTERNAL_SIGNING_SECRETLogin page at localhost:8090VAPID_PUBLIC_KEYlocalhost:3030Cluster crowdvisionExample

From a clean machine to a signed-in user with a first domain. How each tool works is on the Toolchain pages; this page is the order to follow.

-----

What a machine needs

justmiseDocker with ComposeGitopensslNode, Python, Rust, Go, moon, uv, istioctlQuarkdownk3d, kubectlToolEvery command starts with itInstalls the pinned languages and CLIsRuns the local stack. Compose must support include: and --watchClone and branchesEvery .env script makes its keys with itBuild, test and lintOnly for just docs buildOnly for the local clusterWhyBy hand: https://just.systems/By hand: https://mise.jdx.dev/By handBy handBy hand, most systems ship itmise, pins in .mise.toml: Build SystemBy hand, at QUARKDOWN_VERSION from .mise.tomlBy handInstalled by

-----

Install

	git clone https://github.com/NickGhignatti/crowd-vision.git
	cd crowd-vision
	just setup install



245Stepmise downloads each tool in .mise.toml that is missingmoon reads .moon/workspace.yml and starts every project’s deps taskNode: npm ci. Python: uv sync --locked. Rust: cargo fetch. Go: go mod downloadWhat happens

- No step rewrites a lockfile, so an install on macOS or Windows cannot break CI.
- MOON_CONCURRENCY=2 just setup install caps the parallel tasks on a small machine.
- Lockfiles, and why Node locks are made for Linux: Dependencies & Security.

-----

The .env file

	just stack env

Eleven POSIX sh scripts in scripts/env/ run in order. Each one writes only a value missing from .env, so a second run changes nothing. just stack dev and just stack start run it first anyway.

create.shvapid.shtoken.shconfig.shlangfuse.shkeycloak.shcontrolplane.shgateway-key.shingest-key.shtelemetry-db.shrust.shScriptAn empty .env, if none existsVAPID_PUBLIC_KEY, VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY, VITE_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEYEVAL_JWT_SECRET, 256-bit hexBACKEND_PORT (80), FRONTEND_PORT (8080), DEV_URL (http://localhost), and asks for OPENROUTER_API_KEYLangfuse keys, its first-boot admin, the agent’s trace exporter settingsKEYCLOAK_ADMIN_USER (admin), KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD, KEYCLOAK_DB_PASSWORD, empty GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRETINTERNAL_SIGNING_SECRET, TENANCY_DB_PASSWORD, REGISTRY_DB_PASSWORDA 2048-bit RSA key in secrets/gateway-dev-key.pem, not in .envTELEMETRY_DEVICE_MASTER_KEY, TELEMETRY_INGEST_SECRETTELEMETRY_DB_PASSWORDRUST_VERSION, copied from .mise.tomlWritesevery other scriptnotification, frontendagent evaluation runsCaddy, frontend, agentLangfuse, agentKeycloakthe four Go servicesclaims-gatewaytelemetry, simulators, ap-collectorthe cluster only: Compose uses the fixed password telemetrythe rust-base image buildUsed by

What some of these values mean:

- OPENROUTER_API_KEY is the only question the chain asks. Empty is fine: agent starts, and the first question to the assistant fails. Keys: https://openrouter.ai/keys. GOOGLE_API_KEY and DEEPSEEK_API_KEY are read as the same key.
- INTERNAL_SIGNING_SECRET must be one value for all four Go services: each signs or checks the others’ calls with it.
- TELEMETRY_DEVICE_MASTER_KEY makes every building’s device key. Losing it locks out every collector.
- TELEMETRY_INGEST_SECRET signs for any building. Simulators need it. A real site never gets it.
- The gateway key lives in a file because a PEM key spans many lines and a .env value cannot. With no file, claims-gateway makes a new key at each start, and every open session dies.
- Langfuse opens at http://localhost:3030, user admin@crowd-vision.local, password langfuse-admin. Without OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, agent prints its traces to the console instead.

Example: a new key. A teammate loses their VAPID keys:

	sed -i '/^VAPID_\|^VITE_VAPID_/d' .env   # drop the three lines
	sh scripts/env/vapid.sh                  # one script writes them again

ENV_FILE=/path/to/other.env makes every script write to another file.

-----

First start and first login

	just stack dev



- There is no seed script: every account goes through Keycloak.
- The first build compiles every service: about 12 minutes on a 12-core laptop.
- Check the edge is up: curl -i http://localhost/twin/health answers 200.
- Keycloak’s admin console is at http://localhost:8090, with the KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_* values from .env.
- The full list of addresses, and how to leave parts out: Run the Application.

A cold build loads the CPU, not memory
-----
- Measured on a 12-core, 16 GB laptop: just stack dev --build took 728 s, CPU pressure 88–96 % for about eight minutes, free memory never under 7.7 GB.
- Build steps run under system.slice, so a CPUWeight on docker.slice does not slow them. sudo systemctl set-property user.slice CPUWeight=400 keeps the desktop responsive.
- COMPOSE_PARALLEL_LIMIT has no effect: the runner always builds with COMPOSE_BAKE=true.

-----

The local cluster, in short

The full path is on Kubernetes & Istio.

1234StepAdd 127.0.0.1 crowdvision.local to the hosts fileOptional: GHCR_USERNAME, GHCR_TOKEN in .envjust k8s setupOpen http://crowdvision.localCommandjust k8s hosts prints the line. Linux and macOS: /etc/hosts. Windows: C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hostsOnly for private images. The token needs read:packagesk3d cluster with one server, Gateway API, Istio ambient, namespace, secrets from .env, every manifestSame paths as Compose, Grafana includedNote

- Keycloak is not deployed in the cluster, so signing in there fails unless a Keycloak is reachable from it.
- Prometheus has no route: kubectl port-forward reaches it.

-----

Traps

- A value already in .env is never replaced. Rotating one means deleting its line first. Only RUST_VERSION is written again on every run.
- Deleting secrets/gateway-dev-key.pem signs everyone out. The next start makes a new key.
- A lockfile made by a plain npm install on macOS or Windows loses its Linux packages, and CI’s npm ci fails. just setup clean-install makes every Node and Python lockfile again.

-----

Gaps

- keycloak/README-google.md does not exist, though keycloak.sh points to it. How to set up the “Continue with Google” client is written nowhere.
- just k8s build likely fails for the six Rust images. Each Dockerfile starts FROM rust-base. Compose provides it as a build context, but the plain docker build in the recipe gives none, and the local image is named crowd-vision-rust-base. Read from the files, not run.
- openssl, k3d, kubectl and Quarkdown have no pin in .mise.toml: each machine has its own version.
