entries.content:
Run the Application

StackWatchRuntime fileExcludeDetachedWordEvery container of CrowdVision running together on one machineCompose copies a saved file into the running container, or rebuilds itcompose.runtime.yml, written at each start, listing the compose files keptA word that leaves out every folder or service whose name contains itContainers run in the background; the terminal is freeMeaningCaddy, Redis, Kafka, the servicesEdit src/main.rs, telemetry restartsThe input of every just stack and just db recipesimulatorjust stack startExample

How to start, look at, reset and stop CrowdVision on one machine, and on the local cluster. First-time setup comes before: Setting Up the Environment. How Compose is wired: Docker Compose.

-----

Start and stop

just stack devjust stack startjust stack downjust stack logs [service]CommandEverything, with watchEverything, rebuilt, no watchStops and removes every container, ignoring any exclusionFollows the logs, all or oneRunseach docker-compose.yml plus each docker-compose.dev.ymleach docker-compose.yml onlythe last runtime filethe last runtime fileFiles usedStays attachedDetachedReturnsStays attachedTerminal

Both dev and start run just stack env first. What just stack dev does, step by step: Docker Compose.

The dev files add, per service: the watch rules, a database port on the host, and a web page to browse the database.

-----

Leaving parts out

--no-agent--no-metrics--no-simulators--no-devicesAny bare word--build--dry-runFlag or wordThe backend/agent folder: agent, agent-db and Langfuseprometheus, grafanasensor-simulator, aq-simulator, ap-simulatorap-collectorEvery folder and service whose name contains itNothing: rebuilds the images firstNothing: prints the docker compose command and stopsLeaves out

Example. just stack dev --no-simulators frontend:

- Folders skipped: the three in simulators/, and frontend.
- The runner prints excluded: simulators/aq-simulator, and so on, then the command it runs.
- ap-collector still starts: it lives in devices/. It finds no simulated router and posts nothing.

A mistyped word is silent
-----
A mistyped flag stops the run: unrecognized arguments: --no-metrcs. A mistyped word matches nothing, and every service starts. --dry-run shows the list before anything starts.

-----

Addresses

FrontendEdge, every APIKeycloak, sign-in and admin consoleLangfuseGrafanaPrometheusdigital-twin database, Mongo Expresstelemetry database, pgwebnotification database, Mongo Expressdashboard database, Mongo Expresschat database, Mongo ExpressSimulatorsPagehttp://localhost:8080http://localhosthttp://localhost:8090http://localhost:3030, or http://localhost/langfuse, which redirects therehttp://localhost/grafana/http://localhost/prometheus/http://localhost/twin-db-gui/http://localhost/telemetry-db-gui/http://localhost/notification-db-gui/http://localhost/dashboard-db-gui/http://localhost/chat-db-gui/localhost:3001 sensor, :3002 air quality, :3003 routersAddressAlwaysAlwaysAlwaysWithout --no-agentWithout --no-metricsWithout --no-metricsdev onlydev onlydev onlydev onlydev onlyWithout --no-simulatorsWhen

Every database port on the host: Docker Compose.

-----

Resetting data

just db clearjust db clear-telemetryCommandDrops the chat, digital-twin and notification databases. Empties the agent’s documents and chunksEmpties the telemetry tables: readings, thresholds, sensors, rooms, buildingsDoes

- Both act on the last runtime file, so the stack must have been started through just.
- The volumes stay. A full wipe is just stack down, then docker volume rm on the volume.
- tenancy, registry and Keycloak keep their data: an account and its domains survive both commands.

-----

The local cluster

First creation: Setting Up the Environment. Everything else: Kubernetes & Istio.

Running a local change in the cluster



1246Stepdocker build -t ghcr.io/nickghignatti/crowdvision-twin:latest -f backend/digital-twin/Dockerfile .just k8s load: imports all twelve images, so each must exist locallyjust k8s restart digital-twinjust k8s rollout digital-twinCommand

- Every image builds from the repo root with -f backend/<service>/Dockerfile ., except frontend, which builds from ./frontend. The services read sibling folders, such as backend/libs/ and schemas/.
- just k8s build builds all twelve. See the gap about Rust images on Setting Up the Environment.

Day to day

just k8s stopjust k8s startjust k8s statusjust k8s logs digital-twinjust k8s applyjust k8s restart-alljust k8s deletek3d cluster delete crowdvisionCommandPauses the cluster. Pods, volumes and secrets stayResumes itLists pods, deployments, services, StatefulSetsFollows one service’s logsApplies every manifest again. Safe to repeatRestarts every deployment, after a secret changesDeletes the crowdvision namespace and all its data. The cluster staysDeletes the cluster itselfDoes

-----

When something goes wrong

502 from localhostA left-out service starts anywaycompose.runtime.yml not foundA new variable is emptyjust k8s secrets: namespaces not foundPods in ImagePullBackOffWindows: kubectl cannot connect after just k8s startSign-in fails in the clusterWhat is seenCaddy reached a service that is not listening yet, or crashedThe word was mistypedNo just stack run started this stack.env predates itThe namespace does not exist yetThe cluster tries to pull an image it does not haveThe load balancer came back on another portKeycloak is not deployed thereCausejust stack logs <service>. A Rust service compiles for minutes on the first start--dry-run, or the flagStart it with just stack devjust stack env: it adds only what is missingkubectl apply -f k8s/namespace.yml, then againBuild it, then just k8s loaddocker ps --filter name=k3d-crowdvision-serverlb, then kubectl config set-cluster k3d-crowdvision --server=https://127.0.0.1:<port>Point claims-gateway at a reachable KeycloakFix

-----

Other commands

Tests, one service or allLint and formatLockfiles and security checksEvery recipeThis siteLoading the docs into the assistantForTesting ToolsLinting & FormattingDependencies & SecurityBuild System, or just with no argumentjust docs buildjust agent ingest, after editing documentation/Page

-----

Gaps

- sensor-simulator does not reload a code change. Its watch rule rebuilds only on package.json. An edit in src/ needs just stack dev --build.
- sensor-simulator’s dev script runs src/index.js, which does not exist: the code is TypeScript. Compose never runs that script, so nothing breaks.

entries.title: External Simulators
entries.content:
External Simulators

SimulatorTickubusStationRSSIProbeWordA program that pretends to be real hardware, for local runsOne round: every sensor of one building reads onceThe call interface of an OpenWrt routerA phone connected to a routerHow loud a phone is at a router, in dBm. Closer to 0 is louderA short call a phone sends while looking for networksMeaningaq-simulatorEvery 10 sPOST /<sensorId>/ubus(mac, rssi)−62 dBmHeard up to −92 dBmExample

CrowdVision ships three simulators. They are not microservices: they stand in for hardware that, at a real site, sits outside the cluster.

SensorAir qualityRoutersSimulatorsimulators/sensor-simulator/, Nodesimulators/aq-simulator/, Pythonsimulators/ap-simulator/, PythonLocationcrowdvision-simulatorcrowdvision-aq-simulatorcrowdvision-ap-simulatorImageThermostats (temperature), people counters (peopleCount)Air-quality stations (airQuality)OpenWrt routers (router), polled by devices/ap-collectorPretends to be

-----

Why simulators stay outside the cluster

- The k8s manifests describe only the real system. No test tool reaches production config.
- Each simulator sends readings the way a real device does: signed, to /telemetry/ingest.
- telemetry reaches a simulator through a URL in its own setting, SIMULATORS. k8s sets none, so there a start answers 404.

-----

What is simulated

Exactly the sensors placed in the digital twin. A simulator starts empty and simulates only what telemetry sends it at start.

temperaturepeopleCountairQualityrouterDevice kindsensor-simulatorsensor-simulatoraq-simulatorap-simulatorSimulatorOne temperature reading, in the sensor’s roomOne peopleCount reading, in the sensor’s roomOne airQuality reading, in the sensor’s room, with its own drifting stateNo reading: it answers ubus calls with station lists. ap-collector turns them into a Wi-Fi tick, and telemetry counts it into totalDeviceCount and ratioDeviceCountEach tick, per sensor

- Outdoor sensors (no room) are never simulated: readings are keyed by room.
- Two sensors of one kind in one room give two readings for that room each tick.
- Only a start syncs. A sensor added, moved or removed during a run is simulated from the next start.

-----

Start and run

1. A user with the right to edit the building presses Start simulator: PUT /telemetry/simulation/buildings/{id}.
2. telemetry reads the building’s sensors and splits them by device kind, using SIMULATORS.
3. telemetry sends each simulator POST /control/start with its share. An empty list stops that building.
4. sensor-simulator and aq-simulator send one signed batch every 10 s to their TELEMETRY_INGEST_URL.
5. ap-simulator only answers. ap-collector asks it, every 5 s.



13–568, 912StepOnly the building id. telemetry checks the caller may edit it{ buildingId, sensors: [{ sensorId, sensorType, roomId }] }, pinned by schemas/fixtures/simulation-start.jsonRoom boxes and, when placed, router positions. A failed read answers 502{ buildingId, readings: [...] }, signed with TELEMETRY_INGEST_SECRETOne building’s stations per router, signed with the building’s key or TELEMETRY_INGEST_SECRETData

Stop (DELETE) tells every simulator to drop the building. Status (GET) is running when any simulator runs it. The browser never calls a simulator.

-----

Control API

Called by telemetry only. Every simulator’s tests assert the same start body.

POSTPOSTGETMethod/control/start/control/stop/control/status?buildingId=XEndpoint{ buildingId, sensors: [{ sensorId, sensorType, roomId }] }{ buildingId }—BodyReplaces what the building simulates. Empty sensors stops it. Any other key, like a URL or a coordinate, is refusedStops the building. Stopping one never simulated succeeds{ isRunning }Effect

-----

The router simulator

It fakes the routers, not their readings. Stations still travel router → ap-collector → Wi-Fi tick → telemetry, so the real counting runs on simulated data.

Routers

- One fake router per router sensor, at /<sensorId>/ubus. Login collector / collector; any other pair is refused.
- Probe events stream at GET /<sensorId>/ubus/subscribe/hostapd.wlan0, with the session as a bearer token, every 0.5 s.
- The building comes from digital-twin (DIGITAL_TWIN_URL): room boxes, floors and router positions.
- A restart drops every session. ap-collector logs in again.

People

AP_SIM_PHONES_PER_ROOMAP_SIM_PASSERSBY_PER_HOURAP_SIM_PROBE_RANDOM_MAC_FRACTIONSetting4301.0DefaultPhones per roomPeople walking past outside, heard through the wallsShare of probes sent with a random address, as phones doMeaning

- Each phone visits 3–5 spots and stays 2–15 min at each. The next spot is on the same floor 80 % of the time.
- Arrival is around 08:30 and leaving around 17:30, spread like a bell curve: σ 1.0 h and 1.2 h.
- Everything is seeded by the building id: a restart walks the same people.

Signal

Path loss with walls and floors, then noise.

Loudness at 1 mPath loss exponentEach wallEach floor slabSlow shadowingFast fadingGain spread, router / phonePhone joins a routerPhone roamsPhone dropsRouter forgets an idle phoneProbe heardNumber−40 dBm2.2−5 dB−18 dBσ 4 dB, changes over 30 sσ 2 dB per poll±3 dB / ±4 dBat −82 dBm or louderbelow −72 dBm, to a router 8 dB louderbelow −88 dBmafter 300 sat −92 dBm or louderValue

Example, from the defaults before noise. A phone 10 m from a router:

- Open space: −40 − 10 × 2.2 × log10(10) = −62 dBm. It joins.
- One wall between: −62 − 5 = −67 dBm. It still joins.
- One floor between: −67 − 18 = −85 dBm. Too quiet to join, loud enough for its probes to be heard.

Hand tests

POST /debug/kill/{ap}POST /debug/revive/{ap}GET /debug/ground-truth?buildingId=XEndpointThe router stops answering, with 503It answers againWhere every phone really is, to score an estimate againstDoes

What ap-collector reads in dev

devices/ap-collector/collector.dev.json:

pollIntervalSsyncIntervalSendpointTemplateubussubscribeProbesKey515http://ap-simulator:3000/{sensorId}/ubuscollector / collectortrueValueStation lists asked every 5 sRouter list read from telemetry every 15 sSimulated routers have no address of their own, so this fills itRouter loginListen to probe events tooMeaning

Stop. ap-simulator drops the building, so its routers stop answering. The next Wi-Fi tick lists none of them as answered, and telemetry stores nothing for those rooms.

-----

Configuration

TELEMETRY_INGEST_URLTELEMETRY_INGEST_SECRETDIGITAL_TWIN_URLAP_SIM_*TELEMETRY_SERVICE_URLTELEMETRY_SERVICE_SECRETVariablesensor, air qualitysensor, air qualityroutersroutersap-collectorap-collectorRead byhttp://gateway/telemetry/ingestemptyhttp://digital-twin:3000see Peoplehttp://gateway/telemetryTELEMETRY_INGEST_SECRETDefaultWhere readings go. Set by the simulator’s own environment, never by a callerThe shared key that signs for any building. Dev onlyWhere the building’s rooms come fromCrowd size and probe addressesBase for /collector and /observationsSigns the Wi-Fi tickPurpose

sensor-simulator’s numbers are fixed in simulatorService.ts; a change needs a new image.

delaypeopleCountRangetemperatureRangeParameter10000 ms0 to 5018.0 to 30.0DefaultTime between batchesRandom headcount per people counter per tickRandom °C per thermostat per tick, 2 decimalsMeaning

aq-simulator’s physics, scenarios and sensor errors live in physics.py, scenarios.py and errors.py. Its tick is 10 s.

-----

Running the simulators

The three simulators and ap-collector all start with just stack dev.

	just stack dev --no-simulators   # skip the three simulators; ap-collector still runs
	just stack dev --no-devices      # skip ap-collector
	just stack dev aq                # skip only the air-quality simulator

Alone, against a stack on the host:

	docker run -p 3001:3000 --add-host host.docker.internal:host-gateway \
	  -e TELEMETRY_INGEST_URL=http://host.docker.internal/telemetry/ingest \
	  -e TELEMETRY_INGEST_SECRET=<secret> \
	  ghcr.io/nickghignatti/crowdvision-simulator:latest

- Inside a container, localhost is the container itself, so the URL must name the host.
- --add-host is needed on Linux only. Docker Desktop knows host.docker.internal already.
- telemetry must then list the simulator’s URL in SIMULATORS to start it.

-----

Gaps

- sensor-simulator does not reload a code change under just stack dev: its watch rebuilds only on package.json.

entries.title: Agent
entries.content:
Agent

ToolTool callCedarArgsPydanticJSON SchemaRegistryProtocolProjectionUntrusted dataWordA function the model may ask the service to run, described by a JSON schemaThe model saying “please run this tool with these arguments”The shared rule language that decides who may do whatThe Pydantic class that describes a tool’s arguments. It is also what the model readsA Python library that checks data against a class and can print its JSON SchemaA standard description of a JSON shape: names, types, limitsThe one list of tools. The loop looks tools up hereA Python way to say “anything with these attributes counts”, with no base class to inheritKeeping only the fields the model needs from a bigger answerText that may contain instructions meant to fool the model. It is data, never ordersMeaningget_room(building_id, room_id)list_rooms({"building_id":"b1"})Read = member of the domainGetRoomArgsBaseModel, Field{"type":"object","properties":{…}}REGISTRYTool[ArgsT]drop color, keep capacitya document that says “ignore the rules”Example

How to add a tool to agent, from an empty file to a passing test. How the service works inside, and where tools sit in the loop: Agent. Its role in the system: Agent.

-----

A tool is something the language model can ask agent to do: search the docs, read a building, read a sensor. This page shows how to add one, from an empty file to a passing test.

The short version of how it works:

- The loop (app/agent/loop.py) asks the registry for every tool’s description and argument schema, and gives them to the model.
- The model answers with a tool call: a tool name and some JSON arguments.
- The loop checks the arguments with the tool’s Args class, calls the tool’s run, and puts the result back into the conversation as a message.
- The contract is structural. A tool is any object with the right four attributes. There is no base class to inherit.

-----

What happens to a tool, in pictures



If the name is unknown, the arguments fail the check, or run raises, the loop turns that into an error message for the model. Nothing is thrown at the caller. See Running one tool call in Agent.

-----

1. Pick the shape

Before writing code, answer four questions.

1. What does the tool do, in one sentence? That sentence becomes the description the model reads.
2. What inputs does it need? Each input becomes a field of the Args class.
3. What does it return? Keep it small. The result goes back into the model’s context as JSON, where it costs tokens and can distract the model. Drop every field the model does not need.
4. Read-only, or does it change something? There is no confirmation flow for write actions. Keep tools read-only unless authorization, confirmation, audit logging and retry behaviour are designed on purpose.

Worked example for this page. A new tool count_rooms:

One sentenceInputsReturnsRead-only?Question“Count the rooms of one building.”building_id{"building_id": "b1", "room_count": 4}YesAnswer

(count_rooms is made up for this guide. It is not in the codebase. The code below is the real pattern the existing tools follow.)

Note
-----
The twin tools (app/agent/tools/twin.py) are the reference for a tool that touches real data. Each one checks the caller’s rights first, either can_access_domain(ctx.user, args.domain) or get_authorized_building(...), and forwards the caller’s identity downstream with auth_headers(ctx.user), instead of calling digital-twin as nobody. Follow the same shape for any tool that reads or writes real data.

-----

2. Where the file lives

- A single tool with its own focus goes in a new file: app/agent/tools/<name>.py.
- A group of related tools sharing a backend goes in one file. app/agent/tools/twin.py holds four tools that all talk to digital-twin.

Inside a multi-tool file, a divider comment keeps it easy to scan:

	# ─── list_buildings ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

For the example, count_rooms joins the other building tools, so it goes in twin.py.

-----

3. Write the Args class

	from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
	class CountRoomsArgs(BaseModel):
	    building_id: str = Field(description="Unique id of the building (NOT its name).")

This class does two jobs at once:

1. It checks what the model sends. Args(**call.arguments) raises if a field is missing or has the wrong type.
2. It is what the model reads. The registry calls Args.model_json_schema() and hands the result to the model. The class is the model-facing contract.

What the schema of this class looks like to the model (after cleaning):

	{"type": "object",
	 "properties": {"building_id": {"type": "string", "description": "Unique id of the building (NOT its name)."}},
	 "required": ["building_id"]}

Rules that make the model call the tool well:

- Every field gets Field(description=...). The model sees names, types, required fields, defaults, enums, limits and descriptions. A vague description gives a vague call. The example says “NOT its name” because a model easily passes "HQ" where an id is needed.
- Use the right type (str, int, bool, Literal[...], an enum). Pydantic enforces it and the model sees it.
- Add limits where they help. search_docs uses Field(default=5, ge=1, le=10), so the model cannot ask for 500 chunks.
- Keep names plain. building_id, not bldgIdentifier. The model writes these names straight from the schema.
- Resist making everything optional. Required-by-default gives fewer “I forgot to pass that” errors.

What the registry does to the schema

	def _sanitize_tool_schema(schema: dict) -> dict:
	    drop = {"title", "$defs", "definitions", "additionalProperties"}
	    if isinstance(schema, dict):
	        return {k: _sanitize_tool_schema(v) for k, v in schema.items() if k not in drop}
	    if isinstance(schema, list):
	        return [_sanitize_tool_schema(v) for v in schema]
	    return schema

Pydantic adds a title to everything and sometimes $defs and additionalProperties. Function-calling APIs do not need them, so the registry strips them, deep inside the schema too. It keeps the parameter schema as short as possible.

-----

4. Write the tool class

	from app.agent.tools.access import get_authorized_building
	from app.agent.tools.base import ToolContext, ToolResult
	class CountRoomsTool:
	    name = "count_rooms"
	    description = (
	        "Count the rooms of one building. Use when the building_id is known and only the "
	        "number of rooms is needed. For the rooms themselves, use list_rooms."
	    )
	    Args = CountRoomsArgs
	    async def run(self, args: CountRoomsArgs, ctx: ToolContext) -> ToolResult:
	        ...

namedescriptionArgsrunAttributeThe stable id the model writes in a tool call. snake_case and uniqueWhat the tool does and when to use it instead of its neighbours. See belowThe Pydantic class from step 3. The registry turns it into the schemaAn async method with the signature (self, args: <YourArgs>, ctx: ToolContext) -> ToolResultWhat it is

Writing a good description

The model reads this to choose between tools. So say what the tool does and when to pick it over its neighbours. Compare:

- ❌ “Count rooms.” Too thin. The model will guess when to use it.
- ✅ “Count the rooms of one building. Use when the building_id is known and only the number of rooms is needed. For the rooms themselves, use list_rooms.” It names the precondition and points to the sibling tool.

For a tool with a sibling that does something close, say what it is not for. SearchDocsTool does: “Do NOT use for live operational state — use the twin tools for building structure and the sensor tools for live measurements.”

What ToolContext and ToolResult hold

	@dataclass
	class ToolContext:
	    user: AuthUser
	    session: AsyncSession
	    citations: list[Any] = field(default_factory=list)
	@dataclass
	class ToolResult:
	    content: Any
	    is_error: bool = False
	    citations: list[Any] = field(default_factory=list)

- ctx.user is the signed-in caller. ctx.session is an async database session. ctx.citations collects chunks found so far.
- ToolResult.content is what goes back to the model. is_error=True marks a failure the model can read and recover from. citations adds chunks the answer may cite.

About the generic protocol

	class Tool(Protocol[ArgsT]):
	    name: str
	    description: str
	    Args: type[ArgsT]
	    async def run(self, args: ArgsT, ctx: ToolContext) -> ToolResult: ...

Tool is a Protocol that is generic over the tool’s Args type. A tool does not inherit from it. As long as a class has name, description, Args and a matching run, it already counts as a Tool[YourArgs]. The type variable is what lets the type checker see that run(args: CountRoomsArgs, ...) is a valid fit, not a mismatch.

Note
-----
Do not widen the run parameter to BaseModel to “match the protocol”. That defeats the point and loses type safety. Keep it narrow.

-----

5. Implement run

The rights check and the downstream call already exist as helpers. For a building tool, one call does both:

	async def run(self, args: CountRoomsArgs, ctx: ToolContext) -> ToolResult:
	    building, error = await get_authorized_building(args.building_id, ctx)
	    if error is not None:
	        return error
	    assert building is not None
	    rooms = building.get("rooms")
	    return ToolResult(
	        content={
	            "building_id": args.building_id,
	            "room_count": len(rooms) if isinstance(rooms, list) else 0,
	        }
	    )

Line by line:

1. get_authorized_building asks digital-twin for the building with the caller’s own claims, then checks with Cedar that the caller shares a domain with it. It returns (building, None) or (None, an error ToolResult).
2. If there is an error, return it as it is. The model reads messages like building unavailable or inaccessible and can try something else. A missing building and a foreign building give the same message, so a stranger cannot learn that an id exists.
3. assert building is not None is for the type checker: after error is None, the building is there.
4. Project the answer: only the id and a count go back to the model. Not the rooms, not the domains.

If the tool talks to a backend by itself

When there is no helper that fits, follow the same pattern as list_buildings:

	async def run(self, args: ListBuildingsArgs, ctx: ToolContext) -> ToolResult:
	    if not can_access_domain(ctx.user, args.domain):
	        return ToolResult(content="domain unavailable or inaccessible", is_error=True)
	    try:
	        domain = quote(args.domain, safe="")
	        r = await get_with_retry(get_twin_client(), f"/buildings/{domain}", headers=auth_headers(ctx.user))
	    except httpx.HTTPError:
	        return ToolResult(content="digital-twin is unavailable", is_error=True)
	    if r.status_code >= 400:
	        return ToolResult(content=downstream_error("digital-twin", r), is_error=True)
	    try:
	        data = r.json() or []
	    except ValueError:
	        return ToolResult(content="digital-twin returned invalid data", is_error=True)
	    if not isinstance(data, list):
	        return ToolResult(content="digital-twin returned invalid data", is_error=True)
	    # … keep only id, name, accessible domains and room_count of each building
	    return ToolResult(content={"buildings": slim})

The order is the lesson:

1. Authorize first, before any network call.
2. Escape any model-written text that goes into a URL (quote(..., safe="")), so it cannot climb out of the route.
3. Forward the caller’s identity (auth_headers) and use get_with_retry, which retries a network error or a 502, 503, 504 once.
4. Check the answer’s shape before using it. A downstream that returns something odd becomes ... returned invalid data, not a crash.
5. Project the result.

Rules for run

- Return errors as data, do not raise. Use ToolResult(content=<message>, is_error=True). The loop catches uncaught exceptions anyway, but a clean message lets the model recover (try another id, say it does not know). Raising is for genuine bugs.
- Use ctx. ctx.user is the authenticated caller: use it to enforce access before touching sensitive data. Prefer returning new citations through ToolResult(citations=[...]), which the loop adds to ctx.citations (see SearchDocsTool).
- Project the response. When wrapping an HTTP call, return only the fields the model needs.
- Treat tool results as untrusted data. Downstream responses and retrieved documents may contain instruction-like text. Return structured, minimal payloads. Never rely on the model to decide who may see what: authorization is enforced before the data is returned.
- No print. Use the logger: from app.logging import get_logger; log = get_logger(__name__).
- No per-call global state. Shared module-level objects (an httpx.AsyncClient, a retriever) are fine. State of one call belongs in ctx or in local variables.

-----

6. Register the tool

Open app/agent/tools/__init__.py and add two lines. Today it looks like this:

	from app.agent.tools.twin import (
	    GetBuildingTool,
	    GetRoomTool,
	    ListBuildingsTool,
	    ListRoomsTool,
	)
	REGISTRY.register(SearchDocsTool())
	REGISTRY.register(ListBuildingsTool())
	REGISTRY.register(GetBuildingTool())
	REGISTRY.register(ListRoomsTool())
	REGISTRY.register(GetRoomTool())
	# …

Add CountRoomsTool to the import, and one more REGISTRY.register(CountRoomsTool()).

The order does not matter. A duplicate name raises ValueError: tool 'count_rooms' already registered when the app imports, which is on purpose: it catches a copy-paste clash at start, not in the middle of an answer.

After this, the tool appears in REGISTRY.schemas() and the model can call it. Nothing else needs to change: not the loop, not the route.

Note
-----
If the system prompt lists tools by group (it does: building structure, sensor data, devices, platform docs), check that the new tool fits one of the groups in app/agent/prompts.py. A tool the prompt does not mention can still be called, but the model chooses worse.

-----

7. Test it

Three layers, lightest first.

The Args class

If the class has non-trivial checks (a regex, a range, a custom validator), unit-test them under tests/unit/. Skip this for trivial fields.

	import pytest
	from pydantic import ValidationError
	def test_count_rooms_needs_a_building_id():
	    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
	        CountRoomsArgs()

run against a fake backend

Mock the boundary (the HTTP call, the database session), not the tool itself. Then assert on the ToolResult:

- A building the caller may read: room_count is right, and the result is not an error.
- A building of another domain: building unavailable or inaccessible, is_error true, and no second call was made.
- digital-twin down: digital-twin is unavailable.

Look at tests/unit/test_twin_tool_auth.py and test_twin_tool_failure_modes.py for how the existing tools do it.

Through the agent loop

The integration suite has no reusable scripted LLMClient yet. For now, test run at the backend boundary and smoke-test the dispatch through /ask. When a reusable fake model exists, assert the whole tool-call and recovery sequence through Agent.answer.

-----

8. Run the checks

	just lint affected
	just test agent

Tools go through just (or mise exec --), never the ambient PATH. The checks catch many common mistakes: invalid return annotations and ordinary type errors inside run.

The generic Tool[ArgsT] protocol documents the intended link between Args and the run parameter, but the registry stores tools as Tool[Any]. Do not rely on the type checker alone to catch a mismatch between those two. For a non-trivial tool, exercise schema generation and dispatch in a test.

-----

Quick checklist

- A file in app/agent/tools/<name>.py, or grouped with siblings.
- Args is a BaseModel, and every field has Field(description=...).
- The class has name (snake_case, unique), description (with when to use it), Args and an async run.
- run(args: <YourArgs>, ctx: ToolContext) -> ToolResult: narrow types, no widening to BaseModel.
- Errors are returned as ToolResult(..., is_error=True), not raised.
- Anything touching real data authorizes ctx.user first. Write tools have confirmation and audit behaviour.
- Model-written text that goes into a URL is escaped.
- The response is projected to the minimum the model needs.
- Tool results are treated as untrusted data. Authorization is enforced before data is returned.
- Registered in app/agent/tools/__init__.py.
- just lint affected and just test agent pass.
